Et vidi et peperci eis vix valde, et salvavi mihi acinum de botru et plantationem de tribu multa.
Pereat ergo multitudo quae sine causa nata est, et servetur acinus meus et plantatio mea, quia cum multo labore perfeci haec.
Tu autem si adhuc intermittas septem dies alios, sed non ieiunabis in eis,
ibis autem in campum florum, ubi domus non est aedificata, et manduca solummodo de floribus campi, et carnem non gustabis et vinum non bibes sed solummodo flores,
et deprecare Altissimum sine intermissione, et veniam et loquar te cum.
Et profectus sum, sicut dixit mihi, in campum quod vocatur Ardat, et sedi ibi in floribus et de herbis agri manducavi et facta est esca earum mihi in saturitatem.
Et factum est post dies septem, et ego discumbebam supra faenum et cor meum iterum turbabatur sicut et ante.
Et apertum est os meum et inchoavi dicere coram Altissimo et dixi:
O Domine, in nobis ostendens ostensus es patribus nostris in deserto, quando erant exientes de Aegypto et quando veniebant in deserto quod non calcatur et infructuoso, et dicens dixisti:
Tu Israhel audi me, et semen Iacob intendite sermonibus meis.
Ecce enim ego semino in vobis legem meam, et faciet in vobis fructum, et glorificamini in eo per saeculum.
Nam patres nostri accipientes legem non servaverunt et legitima mea non custodierunt. Et factum est fructum legis non periens; nec enim poterat, quoniam tuus erat.
Nam qui acceperunt perierunt, non custodientes quod in eis seminatum fuerat.
Et ecce consuetudo est ut, cum acceperit terra semen vel navem mare vel vas aliud escas vel potus, et cum fuerit ut exterminetur
quod seminatum est vel quod missum est vel quae suscepta sunt, exterminentur haec, susceptoria vero manent. Apud nos si enim non sic factum est.
Nos quidem qui legem accepimus peccantes peribimus et cor nostrum quod suscepit eam,
nam lex non perit sed permanet in suo honore.

Et cum loquor haec in corde meo, et respexi oculis meis et vidi mulierem in dextera parte, et ecce haec lugebat et plorabat cum voce magna, et animo dolebat valde, et vestimenta eius discisa, et cinis super caput eius.
Et dimisi cogitatus in quibus eram cogitans et conversus sum ad eam et dixi ei:
Ut quid fles et quid doles animo? Et dixit ad me:
Dimitte me, dominus meus, ut defleam me et adiciam dolorem, quoniam valde amara sum animo et humiliata sum valde.
Et dixi ei: Quid passa es, dic mihi. Et dixit ad me:
Sterilis fui ego famula tua et non peperi habens maritum annis triginta.
Ego enim per singulas horas et per singulos dies in annis triginta his deprecabar Altissimum nocte ac die.

Et factum est post triginta annos, exaudivit me Deus ancillae tuae et pervidit humilitatem meam et adtendit tribulationi meae et dedit mihi filium. Et iucundata sum super eum valde ego et vir meus et omnes cives mei, et honorificabamus valde Fortem.
Et nutrivi eum cum labore multo.
Et factum est cum crevisset et venissem accipere illi uxorem, et feci diem epuli.
Et factum est cum introisset filius meus in thalamo suo, cecidit et mortuus est.
Et evertimus omnes lumina, et surrexerunt omnes cives mei ad consolandam me, et quievi usque in alium diem usque noctem.
Et factum est cum omnes quievissent ut me consolarentur ut quiescerem, et surrexi nocte et fugi et veni, sicut vides, in hoc campo.
Et cogito iam non reverti in civitatem sed hic consistere, et neque manducabo neque bibam, sed sine intermissione lugere et ieiunare, usque dum moriar.
Et dereliqui adhuc sermones in quibus eram et respondi cum iracundia ad eam et dixi:
Stulta super omnes mulieres, non vides luctum nostrum et quae nobis contigerunt?
Quoniam Sion mater nostra omnium in tristitia contristatur et humilitate humiliata est. Lugete validissime
et nunc quoniam omnes lugemus, et tristes este quoniam omnes contristati sumus. Tu autem contristaris in uno filio.
Interroga enim terram et dicet tibi, quoniam haec est quae debeat lugere tantorum superstes germinantium.
Et ex ipsa initio omnes nati et alii venient, et ecce paene omnes in perditionem ambulant et in exterminium fit multitudo eorum.
Et quis ergo debet lugere magis nisi haec quae tam magnam multitudinem perdidit, quam tu quae pro uno doles? Si autem dices mihi
quoniam non est similis planctus meus terrae, quoniam fructum ventris mei perdidi, quem cum maeroribus peperi et cum doloribus genui,
terra autem secundum viam terrae, abiit quae in ea multitudo praesens quomodo et venit, et ego tibi dico:
Sicut tu cum dolore peperisti, sic et terra dedit fructum suum hominem ab initio ei qui fecit eam.
Nunc ergo retine apud temet ipsam dolorem tuum et fortiter fer quae tibi contigerunt casus.
Si enim iustificaveris terminum Dei, et filium tuum recipies in tempore et in mulieribus conlaudaberis.
Ingredere ergo in civitatem ad virum tuum. Et dixit ad me:
Non faciam neque ingrediar civitatem, sed hic moriar.
Et adposui adhuc loqui ad eam et dixi:
Noli facere sermonem hunc, sed consenti persuaderi-quid enim casus Sion-et consolare propter dolorem Hierusalem.
Vides enim, quoniam sanctificatio nostra deserta effecta est et altare nostrum demolitum est et templum nostrum destructum est,

et psalterium nostrum humiliatum est et hymnus noster conticuit et exultatio nostra dissoluta est, et lumen candelabri nostri extinctum est et arca testamenti nostri direpta est et sancta nostra contaminata sunt, et nomen quod nominatum est super nos paene profanatum est, et liberi nostri contumeliam passi sunt, et sacerdotes nostri succensi sunt et Levitae nostri in captivitate abierunt, et virgines nostrae coinquinatae sunt et mulieres nostrae vim passae sunt, et iusti nostri rapti sunt et parvuli nostri proditi sunt, et iuvenes nostri servierunt et fortes nostri invalidi facti sunt.
Et quod omnium maius, signaculum Sion, quoniam resignata est de gloria sua nunc et tradita est in manibus eorum qui nos oderunt.
Tu ergo excute tuam multam tristitiam et depone abs te multitudinem dolorum, ut tibi repropitietur Fortis et requiem faciat tibi Altissimus, requietionem laborum.
Et factum est cum loquebar ad eam, et ecce facies eius fulgebat valde subito, et species coruscus fiebat visus eius, ut etiam paverem valde ad eam et cogitarem, quid esset hoc.
Et ecce subito emisit sonum vocis magnum timore plenum, ut commoveretur terra a sono. Et vidi,
et ecce amplius mulier non conparebat mihi, sed civitas aedificabatur et locus demonstrabatur de fundamentis magnis. Et timui et clamavi voce magna et dixi:
Ubi est Urihel angelus, qui a principio venit ad me? Quoniam ipse me fecit venire in multitudinem excessus mentis huius, et factus est finis meus in corruptionem et oratio mea in inproperium.
Et cum essem loquens ego haec, et ecce venit ad me angelus qui in principio venerat ad me et vidit me,
et ecce eram positus ut mortuus et intellectus meus alienatus erat, et tenuit dexteram meam et confortavit me et statuit me super pedes meos et dixit mihi:
Quid tibi est et quare conturbaris et quid conturbatum est intellectum tuum et sensus cordis tui? Et dixi:
Quoniam derelinquens dereliquisti me. Ego quidem feci secundum sermones tuos et exivi in campum, et ecce vidi et video quod non possum enarrare. Et dixit ad me:
Sta ut vir, et commonebo te. Et dixi:
Loquere, dominus meus, tantum me noli derelinquere, ut non frustra moriar,
quoniam vidi quae non sciebam, et audio quae non scio.
Aut numquid sensus meus fallitur et anima mea somniat?
Nunc ergo deprecor te, ut demonstres servo tuo de excessu hoc. Et respondit ad me et dixit:
Audi me, et doceam te et dicam tibi de quibus times, quoniam Altissimus revelavit tibi mysteria multa.
Vidit rectam viam tuam, quoniam sine intermissione contristabaris pro populo tuo et valde lugebas propter Sion.
Hic ergo intellectus visionis: Mulier quae tibi apparuit ante paululum,
quam vidisti lugentem et inchoasti consolare eam,
nunc autem iam non speciem mulieris vides, sed apparuit tibi civitas aedificari.
Et quoniam enarrabat tibi de casu filii sui, haec absolutio est:
Haec mulier quam vidisti haec est Sion, quam nunc conspicis ut civitatem aedificatam.
Et quoniam dixit tibi, quia sterilis fuit annis triginta, propter quod erant anni saeculo tria milia, quando non erat in ea adhuc oblatio oblata.
Et factum est post annos tres, et aedificavit Salomon civitatem et obtulit oblationes. Tunc fuit quando peperit sterilis filium.
Et quod tibi dixit quoniam nutrivi eum cum labore, haec erat habitatio Hierusalem.
Et quoniam dixit tibi quod filius meus veniens in suo thalamo mortuus esset et contigisset ei casus, haec erat quae facta est ruina Hierusalem.
Et ecce vidisti similitudinem eius, quomodo filium luget, et tu inchoasti consolare eam de his quae contigerunt. Haec erant tibi aperienda.
Et nunc videns Altissimus, quoniam ex animo contristatus es et quoniam ex toto corde pateris pro ea, ostendit tibi claritatem gloriae eius et pulchritudinem decoris eius.
Propterea enim dixi tibi, ut maneres in campo, ubi domus non est aedificata.
Sciebam enim ego, quoniam Altissimus incipiebat tibi ostendere haec.
Propterea dixi tibi, ut venires in agrum, ubi non est fundamentum aedificii.
Nec enim poterat opus aedificii hominis sustinere in loco, ubi incipiebat Altissimi civitas ostendi.
Tu ergo noli timere neque expavescat cor tuum, sed ingredere et vide splendorem vel magnitudinem aedificii, quantum capax est tibi visu oculorum videre.
Et post haec audies, quantum capit auditus aurium tuarum audire.
Tu enim beatus es prae multis et vocatus es apud Altissimum sicut et pauci.
Nocte autem quae in crastinum futura est manebis hic,
et ostendet tibi Altissimus eas visiones somniorum, quae faciet Altissimus his qui inhabitant super terram a novissimis diebus.
Et dormivi illam noctem et aliam sicut dixerat mihi.
Et factum est secunda nocte, et vidi somnium, et ecce ascendebat de mari aquila, cui erant duodecim alae pennarum et capita tria.
Et vidi, et ecce expandebat alas suas in omnem terram, et omnes venti caeli insuflabant ad eam et nubes ad eam colligebantur.
Et vidi, et de pennis eius nascebantur contrariae pennae, et ipsae fiebant in pennaculis minutis et modicis.
Nam capita eius erant quiescentia, et de medium caput erat maius aliorum capitum, sed et ipsa quiescebat cum eis.
Et vidi, et ecce aquila volavit in pennis suis et regnavit super terram et super eos qui inhabitant in ea.
Et vidi, quomodo subiecta erant ei omnia quae sub caelo, et nemo illi contradicebat, neque unus de creatura quae est super terram.
Et vidi, et ecce surrexit aquila super ungues suos et emisit vocem pennis suis dicens:
Nolite omnes simul vigilare, dormite unusquisque in loco suo et per tempus vigilate,
capita autem in novissimo serventur.
Et vidi, et ecce vox non exiebat de capitibus eius, sed de medietate corporis eius.
Et numeravi contrarias pennas eius, et ecce ipsae erant octo.
Et vidi, et ecce a dextera parte surrexit una penna et regnavit super omnem terram.
Et factum est cum regnaret, et venit ei finis et non apparuit, ita ut non appareret locus eius. Et sequens exsurrexit et regnabat et ipsa multum tenuit tempus.
Et factum est cum regnaret, et veniebat finis eius, ut non appareret sicut prior.
Et ecce vox emissa est illi dicens:
Audi, tu quae toto tempore tenuisti terram, hoc adnuntii antequam incipias non parere:
Nemo post te tenebit tempus tuum, sed nec dimidium eius.
Et levavit se tertia et tenuit principatum sicut priores, et non apparuit et ipsa.
Et sic contingebat omnibus alis singulatim principatum gerere et iterum nusquam conparere.
Et vidi, et ecce in tempore sequentes pennae erigebantur et ipsae a dextera parte, ut tenerent et ipsae principatum; et ex his erant quae tenebant, sed tamen statim non conparescebant.
Nam et aliquae ex eis erigebantur, sed non tenebant principatum.
Et vidi post haec, et ecce non conparuerunt duodecim pennae et duo pennacula.
Et nihil superavit in corpore aquilae nisi tria capita quiescentia et sex pennacula.
Et vidi, et ecce de sex pennaculis divisa sunt duo et manserunt sub capite quod est ad dexteram partem; nam quattuor manserunt in loco suo.
Et vidi, et ecce hae subalares cogitabant se erigere et tenere principatus.
Et vidi, et ecce una erecta est, sed statim non conparuit.
Et secunda, et haec velocius quam prior non conparuit.
Et vidi, et ecce duae quae superaverunt apud semet ipsa cogitabant et ipsae regnare.
Et in eo cum cogitarent, et ecce unum de quiescentium capitum, quod erat medium, evigilabat, hoc enim erat duorum capitum maior.
Et vidi, quomodo conplexa est duo capita se cum
et ecce conversum est caput cum his qui cum ea erant et comedit duas subalares quae cogitabant regnare.
Hoc autem caput percontinuit omnem terram et dominavit qui inhabitant in ea cum labore multo, et potentatum tenuit orbem terrarum super omnes alas quae fuerunt.
Et vidi post haec, et ecce medium caput subito non conparuit, et hoc sicut alae.
Superaverunt autem duo capita, quae et ipsa similiter regnaverunt super terram et super eos qui habitant in ea.
Et vidi, et ecce devoravit caput a dextera parte illud quod est a leva.
Et audivi vocem dicentem mihi: Conspice contra te et considera quod vides.
Et vidi, et ecce sicut leo suscitatus de silva mugiens, et audivi quomodo emisit vocem hominis ad aquilam et dixit dicens:
Audi tu, et loquar ad te, et dicit Altissimus tibi:
Nonne tu es, quae superasti de quattuor animalibus quae feceram regnare saeculi mei, et ut per eos veniret finis temporum meorum?
Et quartus veniens devicit omnia animalia quae transierunt, et potentatum tenens saeculum cum tremore multo et omnem orbem cum labore pessimo, et inhabitabant tot temporibus orbem terrarum cum dolo.
Et iudicasti terram non cum veritate.
Tribulasti enim mansuetos et laesisti quiescentes, odisti verum dicentes et dilexisti mendaces, et destruxisti habitationes eorum qui fructificabant, et humiliasti muros eorum qui te non nocuerunt.
Et ascendit contumelia ad Altissimum et superbia tua ad Fortem.
Et respexit Altissimus super sua tempora, et ecce finita sunt et saecula eius conpleta sunt.
Propterea non apparens non appareas, tu aquila et alae tuae horribiles et pennacula tua pessima et capita tua maligna et ungues tui pessimi et omne corpus tuum vanum,
uti refrigeret omnis terra et relevetur liberata de tua vi et speret iudicium et misericordiam eius qui fecit eam.
Et factum est dum loqueretur leo verba haec ad aquilam, et vidi,
et ecce quod superaverat caput et non conparuit, et alae duae quae ad eum transierunt et erectae sunt ut regnarent, et erat regnum eorum exile et tumultu plenum.
Et vidi, et ecce ipsa non apparescebant, et omne corpus aquilae incendebatur, et expavescebat terra valde. Et ego a multo excessu mentis et a magno timore vigilavi, et dixi spiritui meo:
Ecce tu mihi praestitisti haec, in eo quod scrutas vias Altissimi.
Ecce adhuc fatigatus sum animo et spiritu meo invalidus sum valde, et nec modica est in me virtus a multo timore quem expavi nocte hac.
Nunc ergo orabo Altissimum, ut me confortet usque in finem.
Et dixi: Dominator Domine, si inveni gratiam ante oculos tuos, et si iustificatus sum apud te prae multis, et si certum ascendit deprecatio mea ante faciem tuam,
conforta me et ostende servo tuo mihi interpretationem et distinctionem visus horribilis huius, ut pienissime consoles animam meam.
Dignum enim me habuisti, ostendere mihi temporum finem et temporum novissima. Et dixit ad me:
Haec est interpretatio visionis huius quam vidisti:
Aquilam quam vidisti ascendentem de mari, hoc est regnum quartum, quod visum est in visu Danihelo fratri tuo,
sed non est illi interpretatum, quomodo ego nunc tibi interpretor vel interpretavi.
Ecce dies veniunt, et exsurget regnum super terram et erit timoratior omnium regnorum quae fuerunt ante eam.
Regnabunt autem in ea duodecim reges, unus post unum.
Nam secundus qui incipiet regnare, ipse tenebit amplius tempus prae duodecim.
Haec est interpretatio duodecim alarum quas vidisti.
Et quoniam audisti vocem quae locuta est non de capitibus eius exientem, sed de medio corpore eius,
haec est interpretatio, quoniam post tempus regni illius nascentur contentiones non modicae, et periclitabitur ut cadat, et non cadet tunc, sed iterum constituetur in suum initium.
Et quoniam vidisti subalares octo coherentes alis eius,
haec est interpretatio: Exsurgent enim in ipso octo reges, quorum erunt tempora levia et anni citati, et duo quidem ex ipsis perient
adpropinquante tempore medio, quattuor autem servabuntur in tempore, cum incipiet adpropinquare tempus eius ut finiatur, duo vero in finem servabuntur.
Et quoniam vidisti tria capita quiescentia,
haec est interpretatio: In novissimis eius suscitabit Altissimus tria regna et renovabit in ea multa, et dominabunt terram
et qui inhabitant in ea cum labore multo super omnes qui fuerunt ante hos. Propter hoc ipsi vocati sunt capita aquilae.
Isti enim erunt qui recapitulabunt impietates eius et qui perficient novissima eius.
Et quoniam vidisti caput maius non apparescentem, quoniam unus ex eis super lectum suum morietur, et tamen cum tormentis.
Nam duo qui perseveraverunt, gladius eos comedet.
Unius enim gladius comedet qui cum eo, sed tamen et hic gladio in novissimis cadet.
Et quoniam vidisti duas subalares treicientes super caput quod est a dextera parte,
haec est interpretatio: Hii sunt quos conservavit Altissimus in finem suam, hoc erat regnum exile et turbationis plenum,
sicut vidisti. Et leonem quem vidisti de silva evigilantem mugientem et loquentem ad aquilam et arguentem eam iniustitias ipsius per omnes sermones eius, sicut audisti,
hic est unctus, quem reservavit Altissimus in finem ad eos et impietates ipsorum. Arguet illos de iniustitiis ipsorum et infulciet coram ipsis spretiones eorum.
Statuet enim eos primum in iudicium vivos, et erit cum arguerit eos, tunc corrumpet eos.
Nam residuum populum meum liberabit cum misericordia, qui salvati sunt super fines meos, et iucundabit eos, quoadusque veniat finis, dies iudicii, de quo locutus sum tibi ab initio.
Hoc somnium quod vidisti, et haec interpretatio eius.
Tu ergo solus dignus fuisti scire Altissimi secretum hoc.
Scribe ergo omnia ista in libro quae vidisti, et pones ea in loco abscondito.
Et docebis ea sapientes de populo tuo, quorum scis corda posse capere et servare secreta haec.
Tu autem adhuc sustine hic alios dies septem, ut tibi ostendatur quicquid visum fuerit Altissimo ostendere tibi.

Et profectus est a me. Et factum est cum audisset omnis populus, quoniam pertransierunt septem dies, et ego non fuissem reversus in civitatem, et congregavit se omnis a minimo usque ad maximum et venit ad me, et dixerunt mihi dicentes:
Quid peccavimus tibi et quid iniuste egimus in te, quoniam derelinquens nos sedisti in loco hoc?
Tu enim nobis superasti ex omnibus prophetis, sicut botrus de vindemia, et sicut lucerna in loco obscuro, et sicut portus navi salvatae a tempestate.
Aut non sufficiunt nobis mala quae contigerunt?
Si ergo tu nos dereliqueris, quanto erat nobis melius, si essemus succensi et nos incendio Sion.
Nec enim nos meliores sumus eorum, qui ibi mortui sunt. Et ploraverunt voce magna. Et respondi ad eos et dixi:
Confide, Israhel, et noli tristari, tu domus Iacob.
Est enim memoria vestri coram Altissimo, et Fortis non est oblitus vestri in contentione.
Ego enim non dereliqui vos neque excessi a vobis, sed veni in hunc locum, ut deprecarer pro desolatione Sion, et ut quaererem misericordiam pro humilitate sanctificationis vestrae.
Et nunc ite unusquisque vestrum in domum suam, et ego veniam ad vos post dies istos.
Et profectus est populus, sicut dixi ei, in civitatem.
Ego autem sedi in campo septem diebus, sicut mihi mandavit, et manducabam de floribus solummodo agri, de herbis facta est mihi esca in diebus illis.
Et factum est post dies septem, et somniavi somnium nocte.
Et ecce de mari ventus exsurgebat, ut conturbaret omnes fluctus eius.
Et vidi, et ecce convolabat ipse homo cum nubibus caeli. Et ubi vultum suum convertebat ut consideraret, tremebant omnia quae sub eo videbantur.
Et ubicumque exiebat vox de ore eius, ardescebant omnes qui audiebant voces eius, sicut liquescit quando senserit ignem.
Et vidi post haec, et ecce congregabatur multitudo hominum, quorum non erat numerus, de quattuor ventis caeli, ut debellarent hominem qui ascenderat de mari.
Et vidi, et ecce sibimet ipso sculpsit montem magnum et volavit super eum.
Ego autem quaesivi videre regionem vel locum, unde sculptus esset mons, et non potui.
Et post haec vidi, et ecce omnes qui congregati sunt ad eum ut expugnarent eum, timebant valde, tamen audebant pugnare.
Et ecce ut vidit impetum multitudinis venientis, non levavit manum suam neque frameam tenebat neque aliquod vas bellicosum, nisi solummodo vidi,

quomodo emittit de ore suo sicut fluctum ignis, et de labiis eius spiritum flammae, et de lingua eius emittebat scintillas tempestatis. Et commixta sunt simul omnia haec, fluctus ignis et spiritus flammae et multitudo tempestatis.

Et concidit super multitudinis impetum quod paratum erat pugnare, et succendit omnes, ut subito nihil videretur de innumerabili multitudine nisi solummodo pulvis cineris et fumi odor. Et vidi et extiti.
Et post haec vidi ipsum hominem descendentem de monte et advocantem ad se multitudinem aliam pacificam.

Et accedebant ad eum vultus hominum multorum, quorumdam gaudentium, quorumdam tristantium, aliqui vero alligati, aliqui adducentes ex eis qui offerebantur. Et ego a multitudine pavoris expergefactus sum et deprecatus sum Altissimum et dixi:
Tu ab initio demonstrasti servo tuo mirabilia haec et dignum me habuisti, ut susciperes deprecationem meam.
Et nunc demonstra mihi adhuc et interpretationem somnii huius.
Sicut enim existimo in sensu meo, vae qui derelicti fuerint in diebus illis, et multo plus vae his qui non sunt derelicti.
Qui enim non sunt derelicti, tristes erunt
intellegentes quae sunt reposita in novissimis diebus, et non occurrentes eis. Sed et qui derelicti sunt
propter hoc vae, viderunt enim pericula magna et necessitates multas, sicut ostendunt somnia haec.
Attamen facilius est periclitantem venire in haec, quam pertransire sicut nubem a saeculo et non videre quae contigerunt in novissimo. Et respondit ad me et dixit:
Et visionis interpretationem dicam tibi, sed et de quibus locutus es adaperiam tibi.
Quoniam dixisti de his qui derelicti sunt et de his qui non derelicti sunt, haec interpretatio:
Qui adferet periculum in illo tempore, ipse custodibit qui in periculo inciderint, qui habent operas et fidem ad Fortissimum.
Scito ergo, quoniam magis beatificati sunt qui derelicti super eos qui mortui sunt.
Interpretatio enim visionis haec: Quia vidisti virum ascendentem de corde maris,
ipse est quem conservat Altissimus multis temporibus, qui per semet ipsum liberabit creaturam suam, et ipse disponet qui derelicti sunt.
Et quoniam vidisti de ore eius exire ut spiritum et ignem et tempestatem,
et quoniam non tenebat frameam neque vas bellicosum, corrumpit enim impetum eius multitudinis quae venerat ad expugnare eum, haec interpretatio:
Ecce dies veniunt, quando incipiet Altissimus liberare eos qui super terram sunt.
Et veniet excessus mentis super eos qui inhabitant terram.
Et in alisalio cogitabunt bellare, civitates civitatem et locus locum et gens ad gentem et regnum adversus regnum.
Et erit cum fient haec et contingent signa quae ante ostendi tibi, et tunc revelabitur Filius meus quem vidisti virum ascendentem.
Et erit quando audierint omnes gentes vocem eius, et derelinquet unusquisque regionem suam et bellum quod habent in alterutro,
et colligetur in unum multitudo innumerabilis, sicut vidisti volentes venire et expugnare eum.
Ipse autem stabit super cacumen montis Sion.
Sion autem veniet et ostendetur omnibus parata et aedificata, sicut vidisti montem sculpi sine manibus.
Ipse autem Filius meus arguet quae advenerunt gentes impietates eorum, has quae tempestati adpropiaverunt, et inproperabit coram eis mala cogitamenta eorum et cruciamenta quibus incipient cruciari,
quae adsimilatae sunt flammae, et perdet eos sine labore et legem quae igni adsimilata est.
Et quoniam vidisti eum colligentem ad se aliam multitudinem pacificam,

haec sunt novem tribus, quae captivae factae sunt de terra sua in diebus Iosiae regis, quem captivum duxit Salmanassar rex Assyriorum, et transtulit eos trans Flumen, et translati sunt in terram aliam.
Ipsi autem sibi dederunt consilium hoc, ut derelinquerent multitudinem gentium, et proficiscerentur in ulteriorem regionem, ubi numquam quisquam inhabitavit ibi genus humanum,
ut vel ibi observarent legitima sua, quae non fuerant servantes in regione sua.
Per introitus autem angustos fluminis Eufraten introierunt.
Fecit enim eis tunc Altissimus signa, et statuit venas Fluminis usquequo transirent.
Per eam enim regionem erat via multa itineris anni unius et dimidii, nam regio illa vocatur Arzar, et
tunc inhabitaverunt ibi usque in novissimo tempore. Et nunc iterum coeperunt venire,
iterum Altissimus statuit venas Fluminis, ut possint transire, propter hoc vidisti multitudinem collectam cum pace,
sed et qui derelicti sunt de populo tuo, qui invenientur intra terminum meum
sanctum. Erit ergo quando incipiet perdere multitudinem earum quae collectae sunt gentes, proteget qui superaverit populum.
Et tunc ostendet eis multa plurima portenta.
Et dixi ego: Dominator Domine, hoc mihi ostende, propter quod vidi virum ascendentem de corde maris. Et dixit mihi:
Sicut non potest hoc vel scrutinare vel scire quis, quid sit in profundo maris, sic non poterit quisquam super terram videre Filium meum vel eos qui cum eo sunt nisi in tempore diei.
Haec est interpretatio somnii quem vidisti, et propter quod inluminatus es haec solus.
Dereliquisti enim tua et circa mea vacasti et legem meam exquisisti.
Vitam enim tuam disposuisti in sapientiam, et sensum tuum vocasti matrem.
Et propter hoc ostendi tibi haec, merces apud Altissimum. Erit enim post alios tres dies, ad te alia loquar et exponam tibi gràvia et mirabilia.
Et profectus sum et transii in campum, multum glorificans et laudans Altissimum de mirabilibus, quae per tempus faciebat,
et quoniam gubernat tempora et quae sunt in temporibus inlata. Et sedi ibi tribus diebus.
Et factum est tertio die, et ego sedebam sub quercu,
et ecce vox exivit contra me de rubo et dixit: Ezra, Ezra. Et dixi: Ecce ego, Domine. Et surrexi super pedes meos. Et dixit ad me:
Revelans revelatus sum super rubum et locutus sum Moysi, quando populus meus serviebat in Aegypto.
Et misi eum et eduxi populum meum de Aegypto, et adduxi eum super montem Sina et detinebam eum apud me diebus multis,
et enarravi ei mirabilia multa, et ostendi ei temporum secreta et temporum finem. Et praecepi ei dicens:
Haec in palam facies verba et haec abscondes.
Et nunc tibi dico:
Signa quae demonstravi et somnia quae vidisti et interpretationes quas tu audisti, in corde tuo repone ea.
Tu enim recipieris ab hominibus, et converteris residuum cum Filio meo et cum similibus tuis, usquequo finiantur tempora,
quoniam saeculum perdidit iuventutem suam et tempora adpropinquant senescere.
Duodecim enim partibus divisum est saeculum, et transierunt eius decem iam et dimidium decimae partis,
superant autem eius duae prae medium decimae partis.
Nunc ergo dispone domum tuam, et corripe populum tuum, et consolare humiles eorum, et renuntia iam corruptae vitae,

et dimitte abs te mortales cogitationes, et proice abs te pondera humana, et exue te iam infirmam naturam, et repone in unam partem molestissima tibi cogitamenta, et festina transmigrare a temporibus his.
Quae enim vidisti nunc contigisse mala, iterum horum deteriora facientur,
quantum enim invalidum fieri saeculum a senectute, tantum multiplicabunt super inhabitantes mala.
Prolongavit enim magis veritas et adpropinquavit mendacium. Iam enim festinat aquila venire, quam vidisti in visionem.
Et respondi: Dixi coram te, Domine.
Ecce enim ego abibo sicut praecepisti mihi, et corripiam praesentem populum. Qui autem iterum nati fuerint, quis commonebit?
Positum est ergo saeculum in tenebris, et qui inhabitant in eo sine lumine,
quoniam lex tua incensa est, propter quod nemo scit quae a te facta sunt vel quae incipient operae.

Si enim inveni gratiam coram te, inmitte in me spiritum sanctum, et scribam omne quod factum est in saeculo ab initio, quae erant in lege tua scripta, ut possint homines invenire semitam, et qui voluerint vivere in novissimis vivant.
Et respondit ad me et dixit: Vadens congrega populum et dices ad eos, ut non te quaerant diebus quadraginta.
Tu autem praepara tibi buxos multos et accipe te cum Saream, Dabriam, Selemiam, Ethanum et Asihel, quinque hos qui parati sunt ad scribendum velociter.
Et venies hic, et ego accendam in corde tuo lucernam intellectus, quae non extinguetur quoadusque finiantur quae incipies scribere.
Et cum perfeceris, quaedam palam facies, quaedam sapientibus absconse trades. In crastinum enim hac hora incipies scribere.
Et profectus sum, sicut mihi praecepit, et congregavi omnem populum et dixi:
Audi, Israhel, verba haec:
Peregrinantes peregrinati sunt patres nostri ab initio in Aegypto, et liberati sunt inde.
Et acceperunt legem vitae, quem non custodierunt, quem et vos post eos transgressi estis.
Et data est vobis terra in sortem in terra Sion, et vos et patres vestri iniquitatem fecistis et non servastis vias, quas vobis praecepit Altissimus.
Iustus iudex cum sit, abstulit a vobis in tempore quod donaverat.
Et nunc vos hic estis, et fratres vestri introrsus vestrum sunt.
Si ergo imperaveritis sensui vestro et erudieritis cor vestrum, vivi conservati eritis et post mortem misericordiam consequemini.
Iudicium enim post mortem veniet, quando iterum reviviscemus, et tunc iustorum nomina parebunt et impiorum facta ostendentur.
Ad me autem nemo accedat nunc, neque requirent me usque diebus quadraginta.
Et accepi quinque viros, sicut mandavit mihi, et profecti sumus in campo et mansimus ibi.
Et factus sum in crastinum, et ecce vox vocavit me dicens: Ezra, aperi os tuum et bibe quod te potiono.
Et aperui os meum, et ecce calix plenus porrigebatur mihi; hoc erat plenum sicut aqua, color autem eius ut ignis similis.
Et accepi et bibi, et in eo cum bibissem cor meum eructabatur intellectum et in pectus meum increscebat sapientia. Nam spiritus meus conservabat memoriam,
et apertum est os meum et non est clausum amplius.
Altissimus autem dedit intellectum quinque viris, et scripserunt quae dicebantur ex successione notis quas non sciebant, et sederunt quadraginta diebus. Ipsi autem per diem scribebant,
nocte autem manducabant panem; ego autem per diem loquebar et nocte non tacebam.
Scripti sunt autem in quadraginta diebus libri nongenti quattuor.
Et factum est cum conpleti essent quadraginta dies, et locutus est Altissimus dicens: Priora quae scripsisti in palam pone, et legant digni et indigni.
Novissimos autem septuaginta conservabis, ut tradas eos sapientibus de populo tuo.
In his enim est vena intellectus et sapientiae fons et scientiae flumen. Et feci sic.

ms.name: OCP Translation
ms.bibliography: English translation of Syriac (English) based on the OCP critical edition.

unit.reading: In the thirtieth year after the downfall of our city, I, Shealtiel, who am Ezra,
was in Babylon,
and I was lying on my bed, and was troubled,
and thoughts were coming up into my heart,
because I saw the desolation of Zion
and the prosperity of the inhabitants of Babylon.
And my spirit was greatly stirred,
and I began to speak words of fear to the Most High,
and I said:
“O Lord, my Lord,
did you not speak at the beginning, when you formed the earth—and that alone—
and commanded the dust,
and it gave you Adam, a dead body?
Yet he was the creation of your hands,
and you breathed into him the breath of life,
and he became alive before you.
And you brought him into paradise, which your right hand had planted
before the earth appeared.
And to him you laid down a commandment, and he transgressed it;
and immediately you decreed death upon him and upon his generations.
And from him were born nations and tribes,
and tongues and peoples and clans,
of which there is no number.
And each
nation walked
in their works,
and they acted wickedly and did iniquity before you,
and you did not hinder them.
Again, however, in time you brought a flood upon the earth and upon the inhabitants of the world,
and destroyed them.
And their destruction was alike:
just as death came to Adam,
so also to them came the death of the flood.
Yet you left over one of them with his household,
and from him all the righteous proceeded.
And it happened that when the inhabitants of the earth began to multiply,
and produced many children and nations and great assemblies,
they began again to act more wickedly than the former ones.
And it happened that when they acted wickedly before you,
you chose for yourself one of them whose name was Abraham,
and you loved him, and you revealed the end of the times to him alone,
secretly between you and him at night;
and you established an everlasting covenant with him,
and told him that you would never forsake his seed.
And you gave him Isaac,
and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau.
And you chose Jacob for yourself as an inheritance,
and Esau you hated;
and Jacob became a great multitude.
And when you brought up his seed out of Egypt, you established an everlasting covenant with him.
And you brought them to Mount Sinai.
And you bowed the heavens and shook the earth,
and made tremble
the world,
and caused the depths to shudder,
and troubled the ages.
And your glory passed through the four gates of fire, and earthquake, and wind, and frost,
to give the law to the seed of Jacob,
and the commandments to the offspring of Israel.
Yet you did not take away from them the evil heart,
so that your law might bear fruit in them.
For the first Adam clothed himself with an evil heart,
and transgressed and was overcome,
and also
all
who were born of him.
Thus the disease became permanent: the law was in the heart of the people
along with the evil root;
then what was good departed, and what was evil came.
And the times passed, and the years came to an end.
And you raised up for yourself a servant named David.
And you told him to build a city for your name,
and a house, that offerings from what is yours might be presented to you in it.
And this was done for many years.
Then the inhabitants of the city sinned against you,
and they did nothing new beyond what Adam and all his generations had done,
for they too had clothed themselves with an evil heart.
And you delivered your city into the hands of your enemies.
Then I said in my heart, 'Are the inhabitants of Babylon doing any better,
and is it on this account that you have forsaken Zion?'
And it came to pass, when I came here, that I saw many impieties without number,
and my soul saw many wrongdoers in this thirtieth year,
and my heart was agitated,
because I saw how you endure sinners,
and spare the ungodly,
and have destroyed your people and preserved your enemies,
and have not made known to anyone how your way may be understood.
Has Babylon done better than Zion?
Or have you known any other nation more than Israel?
Or what tribe has believed your covenants as Jacob has?
Yet their reward has not appeared,
and their labor has borne no fruit.
For I have passed through among the nations,
and I have seen that they are now prospering,
and do not remember your commandments.
Now therefore, weigh in a balance our iniquities and those of the inhabitants of the world,
and let the inclination of the balance be seen, which way it tilts.
Or when have the inhabitants of the world not sinned before you?
Or what nation has kept your commandments in such a way?
You may indeed find individual men by name who have kept your commandments,
but a nation you cannot find.
And the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered
and said to me,
“Your heart is utterly dismayed in this world,
and do you wish to comprehend the way of the Most High?”
And I answered and said, “Yes, my lord.”
And he answered again and said to me,
“I have been sent to show you three ways,
and to set before you three parables.
If you can declare one of them to me,
I also will show you
the way that you long to see,
and I will teach you why the heart is evil.”
And I answered and said,
“Speak, my lord.”
And he answered and said to me,
“Go, weigh for me the weight of fire,
or measure for me a measure of wind,
or call back for me a day that has passed.”
And I said to him,
“Who among those born of woman is able to do these things that you have spoken of,
that of me,
that you should ask all these things of me, my lord?”
And he said to me,
“If I had asked you and said to you,
‘How many storehouses are in the heart of the sea?
Or how many springs are at the fountainhead of the deep?
Or how many paths are above the firmament?
Or which are the exits of Sheol?
Or which are the paths of Paradise?’
you would have said to me, ‘I have not gone down into the deep,
nor have I yet gone down into Sheol,
nor have I ever ascended into heaven.’
Now, however, I have not asked you about these things,
but about fire and wind and the day—
things through which
you have passed,
and without which you cannot exist—
and you have not told me about them.”
And he said to me,
“You cannot understand the things that have grown up with you;
how then can your vessel comprehend the way of the Most High?
For in that which is incomprehensible
the way of the Most High was created,
and one who is corruptible in a corruptible world is unable
to know the way of the Incorruptible.”
And when I heard these things,
I fell on my face
and said to him,
“It would have been better for us if we had not come into being,
or that, when we have come, we live in wickedness,
and we suffer and do not know
why we suffer?"
And he answered and said to me,
“The trees of the forest of the plain went forth
and devised a plan,
and said,
‘Come, let us go and wage war against the sea,
that it may recede before us,
and we will make for ourselves another forest.’
The waves of the sea likewise devised a plan and said,
‘Come, let us go up and wage war against the forest of the plain,
so that there also we may make for ourselves another place.’
And the plan of the forest came to nothing,
for fire came and consumed it.
And likewise
also the plan of the waves of the sea,
for the sand stood up and stopped them.
If, therefore, you were their judge,
which of them would you justify, and which would you condemn?”
And I answered and said,
“Both of them devised a vain plan,
for the earth was given to the forest,
and the place of the sea to bear its waves.”
And he answered and said to me,
“You have judged well,
and why have you not judged yourself?
For just as the earth is given to the forest
and the place of the sea to bear its waves,
so also those who dwell upon the earth
are able to understand only what is upon the earth,
and he who is above the heavens, what is above the heavens.”
And I answered and said,
“I beseech you, my Lord,
why, my Lord, was understanding given to me to think?
For I did not wish to ask about the ways above,
but about those things that pass over us every day:
why Israel was given over to the gentiles,
and the people whom you loved was given over to wicked tribes,
and the holy Law of our fathers has been annulled,
and the written covenants are no more;
and we pass away from the world like locusts,
and our life
is like a vapor,
and we are not even worthy to receive mercy.
But what will he do for his great name that has been called upon us?
Concerning these things I asked.”
And he answered and said to me,
“If you remain, you will see;
and if you live long, you will marvel.
because the world is hurrying to pass away,
for it cannot bear to bring what is promised to the righteous.
For this world is full of groaning
and many infirmities.
For the evil about which you asked me has been sown,
and its harvest has not yet come.
Unless, therefore, that which has been sown is reaped, and the place departs
where the evil has been sown,
the land where good is sown will not come.
For a single grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam
from the beginning,
and how much fruit of ungodliness has it produced
until now,
and will produce until the harvest comes!
Consider, then, in yourself and see:
a single grain of evil seed that was sown, how much fruit of ungodliness it has produced!
When, therefore, the countless ears of good things are sown,
how great a harvest will they produce?”
Then I answered and said,
“How long and when will these things be?
For our years are few and evil.”
And he answered and said to me,
“Do not hasten faster than the Most High;
for you hasten on your own account,
but the Most High on behalf of many.
Did not the souls of the righteous in their chambers ask concerning these things,
saying, ‘How long are we to remain here?
And when is the harvest of our reward?’”
And Remiel the angel answered and said to them,
“Until the number of those like you is completed.
For the Holy One has weighed the world in the balance,
and measured the times by measure,
and numbered the seasons by number,
and he will not move nor awaken them until the prescribed number is completed.”
Then I answered and said, “O Lord, my Lord,
yet
behold,
we all are full of ungodliness.
And perhaps on our account the reward of the righteous is withheld,
because of
the sins of those who dwell on the earth.”
And he answered and said to me,
“Go and ask a pregnant woman
whether, when she has completed her nine months,
her womb can still hold the infant within it.”
And I said,
“It cannot, my lord.”
And he answered and said to me,
“Sheol and the chambers of souls are like the womb.
For just as a woman in travail hastens to escape the distress of childbirth,
Even so these also hasten to deliver up that which was placed in them from the beginning.
And then it will be revealed to you concerning those things which you desire to see.”
And I answered and said,
“If I have found favor in your eyes,
and if it is possible, and I am worthy,
make known to me this also:
whether the time that has passed by us is more,
or that which is yet to come.
For the time that has passed I know,
but what is to come I do not know.”
And he answered and said to me,
“Stand on the right side,
and I will show you the interpretation of the parable.”
So I stood and looked,
and behold, a burning furnace of fire passed before me.
And it happened that when the flame had passed by,
I looked, and behold,
there remained
smoke.
And after these things, a cloud full of water passed before me,
and it poured down a very violent rain.
And when the violence of the rain had passed,
drops remained in it.
And he answered and said to me,
“Consider in yourself and see:
just as the rain is more
than the drops, and the fire than the smoke, so has the measure that has passed exceeded;
and the drops and the smoke remain.”
Then I besought him and said,
“Do you think that I shall live until those days?
Or who will be in those days?”
And he answered and said to me,
“Concerning the signs about which you ask me,
I am able to tell you of some of them;
but concerning your life I was not sent to tell you,
for neither do I know.
Now concerning the signs:
behold, days are coming,
and the inhabitants of the earth will be seized with great panic,
and the portion of truth will be hidden,
and the land of faith will be barren.
And iniquity and dissoluteness will increase,
more than this which you see now,
and more than that which you have heard of formerly.
And it will be without stability,
and untrodden, this land which you now see reigning,
and they will see this land made desolate.
And if the Most High grants you
vision,
you will see that which is after the third thrown into confusion;
and the sun shall suddenly shine forth by night,
and the moon by day.
And blood shall drip from wood,
and the stone shall utter its voice,
and the peoples shall be troubled,
and the skies shall be altered.
And one shall reign whom many do not expect,
and the birds shall fly away,
and the Sea of Sodom shall cast forth fish,
and it shall utter its voice by night, which many do not know;
and all shall hear its voice.

And chasms shall open in many places, and fire shall continually break out, and the wild beasts of the field shall wander away from their haunts, and portents shall be brought forth by women, for infants shall be born before they are mature.
And salt waters shall be found in sweet, and friends shall suddenly make war on their friends; and then wisdom shall hide itself, and understanding shall withdraw into its chambers,
and it shall be sought
by many, but shall not be found; and oppression and dissipation shall increase upon the earth.
And one region shall ask another that is near to it and say, 'Has righteousness, or a man who does righteousness, passed through you?' And that region will deny it.
And it shall come to pass in that time that human beings shall hope and not obtain; and they shall strive and not succeed; and they shall labor, but their way shall not prosper.
These signs I was commanded to tell you; and if you pray again and petition as now, and fast seven days, you shall hear yet greater things than these."
Then I awoke, and my body trembled exceedingly, and my soul was so weary that it was as if to depart.
And the angel who spoke with me took hold of me, and strengthened me, and set me upon my feet.
And it came to pass on the second night that Phaltiel, a leader of the people, came to me and said to me, "Where have you been, and why is your face downcast?
Or do you not know that you were entrusted with Israel in the land of their captivity?
Rise up therefore and eat a little bread, lest you forsake them like a shepherd forsaking his flock into the hands of ravenous wolves."

And I said to him, "Depart from me and do not come near me for seven days, and then you shall come to me and I will speak to you." And when I had said this to him, he departed from me. The Prayer of Ezra.
And I fasted seven days, groaning and weeping, just as Ramiel the angel had commanded me.
And it came to pass after seven days, that behold, the thoughts of my heart were again very grievous to me.
And my soul recovered the spirit of understanding, and I began again to speak words of petition and supplication before the Most High.
And I answered and said, "O Lord, my Lord, from all the forests of the earth and its trees you have chosen for yourself one vine;
and from all the lands of the world you have chosen for yourself one region;
and from all the depths of the sea you have filled for yourself one stream; and from all
the flowers
of the world you have chosen for yourself one flower; and from all the cities that have been built you have consecrated Zion for yourself;
and from all the birds that were created you have named for yourself one dove; and from all the flocks that were created you have chosen for yourself one sheep;
and from the multitude of nations you have brought near to yourself one people; and the law that was approved above all you gave to the people whom you loved.
And now, Lord, why have you surrendered the one to the many, and dishonored the one root more than the many, and scattered and dispersed your only one among the many?
And those who oppose your commandments have trampled upon those who believed in your covenant.
And if you truly hate your people, it were fitting that they should be punished by your own hands."
And after I had spoken these words, the angel who had been sent to me on the preceding night was sent to me,
and he said to me, "Listen to me, Ezra, and I will instruct you; and look upon me, and I will set forth words before you."
And I answered and said to him, "Speak, my Lord." And he said to me, "Are you so greatly troubled concerning Israel? Or do you love him more than his Maker does?"
And I said, "No, my Lord, but in my sorrow I have spoken; for my reins torment me every hour as I seek to comprehend the judgment of the Most High and to search out something of his justice."
And he said to me, "You cannot." And I said to him, "Why, my Lord?
I pray,
why then was I born? And why did not my mother's womb become my grave, that I might not see the travail of Jacob and the weariness of the offspring of Israel?"
And he answered and said to me, "Count for me those who have not yet come, and gather for me the drops that are scattered, and make green for me the flowers that are withered;

and open for me the chambers that are shut, and bring out for me the winds that are imprisoned in them; and show me the likeness of faces that you have not yet seen, or show me the likeness of a voice; and then I will make known to you the travail and the time that you seek to see."
And I said, "O Lord, my Lord, who is able to know these things except one whose dwelling is not with human beings?
As for me, I am foolish and wretched; how can I speak concerning these things that you have asked me?"

And he said to me, "Just as you are not able to do one of these things that have been mentioned, even so you cannot find out my judgment or the fullness of the love that I have promised to my people."
And I said, "Yet, Lord, behold, you have made promise to those who exist at the end; but what shall they do who were before us, or we ourselves, or those who come after us?"
And he answered and said to me, "I have likened my judgment to a circle; just as there is no lateness for the last, so there is no precedence for the first."
And I answered and said, "Could you not have made together those who have been, those who are, and those who are yet to be, so that you might make your judgment known quickly?"
And he answered and said to me, "Creation cannot hasten faster than its Creator; neither could the world bear all those who were to be created in it at once."

And again I answered and said, "And how did you say to your servant that you will certainly give life all at once to the creation that was created by you? If therefore they will indeed live all at once and creation will endure it, it could even now endure those who are coming into being all at once."
And he answered and said to me, "Ask the womb of a woman, and say to it, 'If you bear ten children, why do you bear them one by one?' Demand of it therefore that it give birth to ten at one time."
And I said, "It cannot, my lord, except at intervals."
And he said to me, "So also have I made the earth a womb for those who come upon it at intervals."
"For just as an infant does not give birth, nor she who has grown old any longer, so also have I ordered the world that I created."

And I asked him and said, "Seeing that you have now given me the way to speak before you: is our mother Zion, of whom you spoke to me—yes, my lord, is she still young, or is she now already nearing old age?"
And he answered and said to me, "Ask a woman who gives birth, and she will tell you."
"Say to her: 'Why are those whom you bear now unlike the earlier ones, but smaller in stature?'"
"And she will say to you, 'Those who were born in the strength of youth are of one sort, and those born in old age, when the womb begins to fail, are of another.'"
"Consider therefore, you also, and see that you are smaller in stature than those who were before you;"
"and those who come after you will be smaller still than you, because creation is already growing old and the vigor of its youth has passed away."
And I answered and said, "I beseech you, my lord, if I have found favor before you, make known to your servant through whom you will visit your creation."

And he answered and said to me, "The beginning was through the Son of Man, but the end is through my own hands. For just as before the earth of the world existed, and before the exits of the world were established, and before the weight of the winds blew,"
"and before the sound of the thunders was heard, and before the flashes of the lightnings shone, and before the land of paradise was confirmed,"
"and before the beauty of the flowers appeared, and before the power of the earthquakes was strengthened, and before the countless hosts of angels were gathered,"
"and before the heights of"
"the air were exalted,"
"and before the measures of the firmaments were named, and before the footstool of Zion was established,"
"and before the present years were reckoned, and before the follies of present sinners were fashioned, and before those who gathered treasures of faith were sealed—"
"even then I deliberated, and all these things came into being through my hands alone, and not through the hands of another."
And I answered and said, "What will be the division of the times? Or when will be the end of the first age, or what will be the beginning of the second?"
And he answered and said to me, "From Abraham to Abraham; from Abraham was born Isaac, and from Isaac were born Jacob and Esau, and Jacob's hand held the heel of Esau."
"For Esau is the heel of the first, and Jacob is the hand of the second."
"For the beginning of a man is his hand, and the end of a man is his heel. Between the heel and the hand, therefore, seek nothing else, O Ezra!"
And I answered and said, "O Lord, my Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes,"
"make known to your servant the completion of the signs, of which you showed me a part on a previous night."
And he answered and said to me, "Rise to your feet, and you will hear a loud voice."
"And it shall be that if the place on which you stand should shake violently,"
"while it speaks with you, do not be terrified, for the word is about the good news of the end; and the foundations of the earth will understand"
"that the word concerns them, and they will tremble and quake, for they perceive that their end is being changed."
And it came to pass, when I heard it, I stood up on my feet; and I listened, and behold, a voice was speaking, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.
And it said, "Behold, the days are coming, and it will be, when I draw near to visit the inhabitants of the earth,"
"and when I am about to require retribution by the hands of the wicked, and when the humiliation of Zion is fulfilled,"
"and when this age which is about to pass away is sealed, these signs I will do: the books will be opened before the face of the firmament, and they will all see my judgment together."
"And one-year-old infants will speak and lift up their voices, and pregnant women will give birth untimely to infants of three and four months, and they will live and leap about."
"And suddenly places that were not"
"sown"
"will be found sown, and storehouses that were full will suddenly be found empty."
"And a trumpet will sound with a loud voice, which all will suddenly hear and be terrified."

"And it will be at that time that friends will make war against their friends like enemies, so that the earth with its inhabitants will be astonished; and the springs of fountains will stand still, so that they will not flow for three hours."
"And it will be that whoever survives all these things that I have foretold to you will be saved and will see my salvation and the end of the world."
"And then they will see the men who were taken up, who have not tasted death from their birth; and the heart of the inhabitants of the earth will be changed and transformed into a different mind."
"For evil will be blotted out, and deceit will be extinguished."
"Faith will flourish, corruption will be overcome, and truth will be revealed, which has remained without fruit for many years."
And it came to pass, while he was speaking with me, behold, little by little the place on which I stood was shaking.
And he said to me, "These things I have come to show you this night."
"If therefore you will pray again and fast for seven days, I will again reveal to you things greater than these."
And be-
cause
your voice was heard before the Most High; for the Mighty One has seen your uprightness and also the holiness that you have had since your youth.
And on account of this he has sent me to reveal to you all these things. And he said to me: Take courage, and do not fear.
And do not hasten to think evil thoughts concerning the earlier times, lest you face judgment in the latter times.
And it came to pass after these things that I wept and fasted seven days, so that I might complete the three weeks that were told to me.
And it came to pass on the eighth night, behold, my heart was again troubled within me, and I began to speak before the Most High.
For my spirit was greatly inflamed, and my soul was in distress.
And I said, 'O Lord, my Lord, you indeed spoke from the beginning of your creation on the first day, and said that heaven and earth should come to be; and your word, Lord, accomplished the work.
And then the Spirit was hovering, and darkness was covering, and there was a silence of sound, and the voice of a human being did not yet exist.
Then you commanded that a ray of light should come forth from your own storehouses, so that your works might be seen.

And again on the second day you created the spirit of the firmament, and commanded it to make a division between waters and waters, so that a part of them should ascend above, and the other part should remain below.

And on the third day you commanded the waters to be gathered together into one of the seven parts of the earth; but six parts you dried and preserved, so that from them some might serve before you, and be cultivated and sown.
And your own word went forth, and in that very hour the work was accomplished.

For then suddenly there sprang up fruits in great abundance without number, sweet in their tastes of every kind, and flowers of diverse appearances that were not alike to one another, and trees incomparable in their appearance, and fragrances inscrutable in their perfumes. These came to be on the third day.
And on the fourth day you commanded, and there came to be the shining sun, and the brightness of the moon, and the order of the stars.
And you commanded them to serve the human being who was to be formed by you.
And on the fifth day you spoke to the seventh part where the waters were, that it should bring forth beasts and winged birds and fish.
And the waters, being speechless and lifeless, produced that which has life, so that from these the generations might recount your wondrous deeds.
And then you preserved two living creatures that you had created; and you called the name of the one Behemoth, and the name of the other you called Leviathan.
And you separated them one from the other, for that wet seventh part was not able to hold them both.
And you gave to Behemoth one of the parts that was dried on the third day, that he might dwell there, where there are a thousand mountains.
And to Leviathan you gave one of the seven parts of moisture; and you preserved them to be food for whomever you will, and whenever you will.
And on the sixth day you commanded the earth to bring forth before you domestic animals and wild beasts and creeping things;
and over these you appointed Adam as ruler over all the works that you had created beforehand; and from him are we, the people whom you have chosen.
All these things I have spoken before you, O Lord, my Lord, because you said that for our sake you created this world.
As for the rest of the nations who were born of Adam, you said that they are nothing, and you compared them to spittle, and like a drop from a bucket you have reckoned their abundance.
And now, Lord, behold, these nations that were considered as nothing, behold, they rule over us and trample us down.
And we, your people, whom you have honored and called your firstborn, only-begotten, near, and beloved, behold, we are handed over into their hands.
And if the world was created for our sake, why do we not inherit our world? How long shall these things be?'
And it came to pass after I had finished speaking these words, behold, there was sent to me the angel who had been sent to me on the former nights.
And he said to me, 'Arise, Ezra, and hear the words that I have come to speak to you.'
And I said to him, 'Speak, my lord.' And he answered and said to me, 'Suppose a sea is situated in a spacious place, so that it is wide and limitless,
but its entrance is situated in a narrow place, so that it is like a river.
Now if anyone should desire to enter the sea and see it, and become master over it, if he does not pass through the narrow place, how is he able to come into the broad place?'
'Hear also another thing: There is a city built and situated in a great place of a plain, and that city is full of many good things;
and its entrance is narrow and situated on a height, so that there is fire on the right hand and deep water on the left;
and one path is set between both of these, between the fire and the water, such that the path is sufficient only for the sole of a man's foot alone.
Now if that city is given as an inheritance, if that heir does not pass through the danger that is set before him, how will he be able to receive his inheritance?'
And I said to him, 'Yes, so it is, my lord.' And he answered and said to me, 'So also is the portion of Israel.
For on their account I made the world; and when Adam transgressed my commandments, that which had been made was condemned.
And on account of this the entrances of this present world have become narrow, and full of sighs and toil and great danger, and heavy weariness along with sicknesses and sorrows.
But the entrances of that world to come are spacious and secure, and they produce fruits that do not die.
If therefore the living do not pass through these narrow and evil things, they are not able to receive what is laid up for them.
Now therefore, why are you shaken, seeing that you are corruptible? And why are you troubled, seeing that you are mortal?
And why have you not taken to heart what is to come, but rather what is present?'
And I answered and said, 'O Lord, my Lord, but behold, you have declared in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the wicked shall perish.
The righteous therefore readily endure hardships, because they hope to come into the broad place; but the wicked suffer hardships, yet do not see the broad place.'
And he answered and said to me, 'You are not
wiser'
more than God, nor
wiser
more than the Most High.
Therefore let the many perish who have come, because the law that was set by me was despised by them.
For God strictly commanded those who came, when they came, what they should do to live, and what they should keep so as not to be tormented.
Yet they rebelled and did not obey him, and formed for themselves vain thoughts.
And they added to themselves deceitful crafts; and in addition to all these things they said that the Most High does not exist, and they did not know his ways.
And they despised his law,
and his covenants
they denied,
and his commandments
they did not trust, and they held his works in contempt.
Therefore, O Ezra: empty things for the empty, and full things for those that are full.

For behold, the days are coming, and it shall be, when the signs that I told you beforehand come to pass, the bride shall be revealed, appearing as a city, and that which is now withdrawn shall be seen.
And everyone who is delivered from these evils that were foretold, he shall see my wonders.
For my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those who are with him, and he shall rejoice those who remain for thirty years.
And it shall be after these years, my son the Messiah shall die, and all who have human breath.
And the world shall be turned back to its primeval silence for seven days, as it was in the beginning, so that no one is left.
And it shall be after seven days, that the world which is not now awake shall be awakened, and corruption shall die.
And the earth shall give up those who sleep in it, and the dust shall give up those who rest in it, and the chambers shall give up the souls that were entrusted to them.
And the Most High shall be revealed upon the throne of judgment; and the end shall come, and mercies shall pass away, and compassion shall depart, and longsuffering shall be withdrawn.
And my judgment alone shall remain, and truth shall stand, and faithfulness shall triumph.
And work shall follow, and reward shall be made known, and righteous deeds shall awaken, and ungodly deeds shall not sleep.
And the pit of torment shall appear, and opposite it the place of rest; the furnace of Gehenna shall be revealed, and opposite it again the paradise of delights.
And then the Most High shall say to those nations that have been raised: 'Look and see whom you have denied, or whom you have not served, or whose commandments you have despised.
Look therefore before you: behold, here are rest and delight, and there are fire and torment.' These things he shall say to them on that Day of Judgment.
For that Day of Judgment is such: there is neither sun in it, nor moon, nor stars,
nor clouds, nor lightning, nor thunder, nor winds, nor water, nor air, nor darkness, nor evening, nor morning,
nor summer, nor winter, nor spring, nor heat, nor frost, nor cold, nor hail, nor dew, nor rain,
nor midday, nor night, nor daytime, nor light, nor brightness, nor shining, nor radiance, but only the ray of the glory of the Most High, by which all are destined to see what has been prepared.
Its duration shall be as a week of years.
This is
my judgment
and its order, and to you alone have I made them known.
And I answered and said: 'Lord, my Lord, I said it then and now I say it again: Blessed are all those who have come and kept the commandments that were laid down by you.
But concerning those for whom my prayer was made: for who among those who have come has not sinned, or who among those born has not transgressed your commandment?
And now
I see
that the world to come is destined to bring delight to few, but to many
torment.

For an evil heart has been in us, which led us astray from these things, and brought us into corruption and showed us the paths of death, and made known to us the ways of destruction, and removed us far from life—and this not to a few, but nearly to all who have existed!'
And he answered and said to me: 'Listen to me, Ezra, and I will speak to you, and instruct you yet again.
For this reason the Most High did not make one world, but two.
For as for you saying that the righteous are not many, but few, hear concerning these things:
If you had precious stones, and they were few, in proportion to their number would you prepare for yourself lead and clay?
And I said: 'How is that possible, my lord?'
And he answered and said to me: 'Not only this, but ask the earth and she will tell you, and speak to her and she will recount to you.
Say to her: You bring forth gold and silver and bronze, and iron and lead, and clay.
Now silver is more abundant than gold, and bronze than silver, and iron than bronze, and lead than iron, and clay than lead.
Judge therefore yourself and consider: which things are precious and desirable, those that are abundant or those that are rare?'
And I answered and said, "O Lord, my Lord, the things that are plentiful are cheap, and the few are precious."
And he answered and said to me, "Consider then in yourself what you have thought, because everyone who has a little rejoices more over what is little than over what is plentiful.
Such is the promise
of my judgment.
For I rejoice and take delight in the few who are saved, because it is they who now establish my glory, and on whose account my name is now praised.
And I am not grieved over the multitude of those who perish, for they are those who now are likened to vapor, and are counted as smoke, and are compared to a flame that burned and was extinguished."
And I answered and said, "O earth, what have you done, that these were born from you and are going to perdition? For if
the mind
comes from the dust, like the rest of the creatures,
it would have been better if even the dust itself had not been, so that
the mind
might not have come from there.
But now the mind grows with us, and on this account we are tormented, because knowing, we perish.
Let the generations of human beings mourn, but let the wild beasts of the field rejoice; let all who are born weep, but let the cattle and the flocks delight,
for it is much better for them than for us, because they do not look for a judgment, nor do they know torment, nor has life after death been promised to them.
For what does it profit us that living we live, but tormenting we are tormented?
For all who are born are entangled in sins, and are full of iniquity, and their falls are heavy upon them.
And if after death we were not to come to judgment, it would have been much better for us."
And he answered and said to me, "When the Most High made the world, and Adam and all those who came from him, he first prepared the judgment and the things
pertaining to the judgment
themselves.
And now understand from your words, for you said that the mind grows with us.

Therefore the inhabitants of the earth are tormented for this reason, that while they possessed a mind they acted wickedly, and received commandments and did not keep them, and they also violated the law that was set for them.
What then will they have to say at the judgment, or how will they open their mouths and speak in the last time?
For how long a time has the Most High been patient with the inhabitants of the world, and not on their own account, but on account of the times that have been appointed?"

And I answered and said, "If I have found mercy before you, O Lord, my Lord, make this known also to your servant: whether after death now, when each one of us gives up our soul, whether we are kept in rest until those times come in which you will renew your creation, or are we tormented from now on?"
And he answered and said to me, "I will make known to you also concerning this; but you, do not join yourself with the rebellious, nor count yourself among those who are tormented.
For you have a treasure of works laid up with the Most High, and it will not be shown to you until the last times.

Now concerning death, this is the word: when the decree of the sentence goes out from the Most High concerning a person that he should die, when the soul is separated from the body, that it may be sent to the one who gave it, first it worships the glory of God.
And if it is of the oppressors, or of those who did not keep the ways of the Most High, or of those who hated those who fear God,
these souls do not enter into the storehouses, but from now on they exist in torment, and they groan and are grieved in seven ways:
The first way: that they rebelled against the law of the Most High.
The second way: that they are unable to turn and do good works by which they might live.
The third way: that they see the reward that is laid up for those who have believed.

The fourth way: when they know and understand the torment that is prepared for them in the end, in which the souls of the ungodly are reproached, because when they had time to serve, they did not subject themselves to the commandments of the Most High.
The fifth way: that they see the storehouses of other souls being guarded by angels in great rest.
The sixth way: that they see the torment that is prepared for them from now on.
The seventh way, which is greater than all these ways that have been mentioned before: that they pine away
in shame,
and are consumed with reproach, and wither in fear as they see the glory of the Most High, before whom they sinned in their life, and before whom they are about to be judged in the end.
Now concerning those who kept the way of the Most High, this is the way when the day arrives that they are separated from this corruptible vessel:
for in that time when they dwelt in it, they served the Most High with labor, and endured danger every hour in order that they might perfectly keep the law of him who gave them the law.
Therefore, this is the word concerning them:
First of all, they see with great joy the glory of the Most High who leads them, and they are refreshed and proceed in seven ways:
The first way: because with great labor they strove to overcome the evil thought that was fashioned with them, that they might not go astray from life unto death.
The second way: that they see the wandering wherein the souls of the ungodly wander and are tossed about, and the torment that is kept for them.
The third way: that they see the testimony that their Fashioner testifies concerning them, because in their life they kept the law that was entrusted to them.

The fourth way: that they see and understand the rest which they now have when gathered in their storehouses, being refreshed in great rest and guarded by angels, and the glory that is kept for them in the end.

The fifth way: that they rejoice over how they have now escaped from what is corruptible, and how they inherit what is to come; and again they see the affliction and the abundance of labor from which they have been freed, and the wide spaces that they are about to receive, and the delights that they will take, becoming immortal.
The sixth way: when it is shown to them how their faces are about to shine like the sun, and how they are about to be made like the light of the stars, and no longer be corruptible.

The seventh way, which is greater than all those that have been mentioned before, is that they exult with boldness, and take courage and are not put to shame, and are eager to see the face of him whom they served in their life, and from whom they are to be glorified, and from whom they are to receive a reward.

These are the ways of the souls of the righteous, which from now on are announced. And the ways of torment that were mentioned before, the rebellious will receive from now on; these souls do not enter the chambers, but from now on they are tossed about in torment, and groan and mourn in seven ways.
And I answered and said, 'Therefore, will there be given
to them
space or time for the souls, after they are separated from the bodies, to see what you have told me?'
And he answered and said to me, 'Seven are the days
of their freedom,
that in those seven days they may see these things that were mentioned beforehand, and afterward they will be gathered into their chambers.'

And I answered and said, 'If I have found mercy in your eyes, show your servant this also: whether on the day of judgment the righteous will be able to intercede for the ungodly, or to pray for them to the Most High,

or fathers on behalf of their children, or children on behalf of their fathers, or brothers on behalf of their brothers, or relatives on behalf of their relatives, or friends on behalf of their beloved friends?'

And he answered and said to me, 'Because you have found mercy before my eyes, I will also make this known to you: the day of judgment is a decisive day, and displays to all the seal of truth. For just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his slave, or a friend his beloved, to be sick in his place, or to sleep, or to eat, or to be healed,
so then also no one can pray on behalf of anyone on that day, nor can anyone lay a burden on another, for everyone then will bear, each one his own righteousness or his own unrighteousness.'
And I answered and said, 'And how, my lord, do we find that Abraham prayed first for the Sodomites, and Moses in the wilderness for the fathers when they sinned,
and Joshua the son of Nun after him for Israel in the days of Achar,
and Samuel in the days of Saul, and David for the destruction of the people, and Solomon for those at the sanctuary,
and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead that he might live,
and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many on behalf of many?'
If therefore now, when corruption was great and oppression increased, the righteous prayed for
the ungodly,
why, my lord, will it not be so then also?'
And he answered and said to me, 'This world has an end, and the glory of God does not remain continually in it. Therefore the strong prayed for those who have no strength.
But the day of judgment is the end of this world, and the beginning of the future world which is immortal, in which corruption passes away,
and dissoluteness is dissolved, and unbelief is abolished, and righteousness increases, and truth shines forth.
Then, therefore, no one can have mercy on the one who was condemned in the judgment, nor harm the one who was victorious in the judgment.'
And I answered and said, 'This is my first and last word: that it would have been better for the earth not to have produced Adam, or when it had produced him, to have restrained him from sinning.
For what advantage is there for all who have come, that behold, they live in distress, and when they have died, they await torment?
O what have you done, Adam? For though it was you who sinned, the evil was not yours alone, but also ours who are descended from you.
For what
profit is there, that behold, an immortal time was promised to us, but we have done mortal deeds?
And that an imperishable hope was made known to us, but we have wickedly become destitute?
And that behold, chambers are kept without care and without sickness, but we have conducted ourselves evilly?
And that the glory of the Most High is to protect those who have lived in chastity, but we have walked in evil ways?
And that Paradise is to be shown, whose fruit does not spoil, in which are delights and healing,
but we shall not enter, because we have served evil places?
And that the faces of the holy ones are to shine brighter than the stars, but our faces will be blacker than darkness?
For we did not consider in our lives, while committing iniquity, that we were going to suffer after our death.'
And he answered and said to me, 'This is the meaning of the contest which the human being who is born struggles upon earth:
if he is defeated, he will suffer what you have said; but if he conquers, he will receive what I have said.

For this is the way that Moses spoke when he was alive to the people, saying to them, "Behold, I have set before you today life and death, good and evil; choose therefore life, that you may live, you and your seed."
Yet they rebelled and did not obey him, nor the prophets after him, nor even me who spoke with them.
Therefore there will not be grief over their destruction, as there will be joy over the life of those who obeyed.'
And I answered and said to him, 'I know, my lord, that now the Most High is called merciful, because he has mercy on those who have not yet come into the world;
and gracious, because he is gracious to those who turn to his law;
and patient, because he shows patience with us, with those who sin, because we are his works;
and generous, because he prefers to give rather than to demand;
and very merciful, because he increasingly multiplies mercy upon those who are now, and upon those who have passed away, and upon those who are to come.
For if he were not to multiply his mercies, the world could not live with its inhabitants;
and giving, because if he did not give out of his goodness, so that the wicked might be lightened of their iniquities, not one of ten thousand of humankind could live;
and a judge,

because if he did not forgive the souls of those who were created by his word, and blot out the multitude of their iniquities, there would not be left of the countless multitude anything except very few.'
And he answered and said to me, "The Most High made this world for the sake of many, but the world that is to come for the sake of few.

Now I will explain a matter before you, O Ezra. Just as you might ask the earth, and it would tell you that it yields much of the dust from which pottery is made, but little of that from which gold is made, so also is the course of this world.
Many have been created, but few shall be saved."
And I answered and said, "Drink up knowledge, O my soul, and consume understanding, O my heart!
