For you came without your will, and you depart though you do not wish; for no authority was given to you except only to live for a short time.

O Lord, my Lord, if you command your servant, I will pray before you: give us seed, and the cultivation of a new heart, from which fruit may come, so that everyone who is corruptible, who has put on the likeness of a human being, may be able to live.
For you are one, and we are one creation, the work of your hands, as you have said.

And you truly give life now in the womb to the body which you have fashioned, and you arrange the limbs; and your creation is preserved in fire and water, and for nine months your fashioned creature endures the creation which you have created within it.
Both that which preserves and that which is preserved are preserved by your keeping; and when the womb yields again what has been formed in it,
you have commanded that from the limbs themselves there should be milk, the fruit of the breasts of fullness,
so that what has been fashioned may be nourished for a little while, and afterward you guide it in your mercy.
And you nourish it in your righteousness, and discipline it in your law, and instruct it in your wisdom.
And you put it to death as your creation, and make it alive as your work.
If then you should quickly and easily destroy this one who was fashioned at your command with all this great labor, why then was he made?
Now too, I have spoken concerning every human being; but more especially—as you know—it is concerning your people that I grieve,
and concerning your inheritance over which I mourn, and concerning Israel for whom I am sorrowful, and concerning the seed of Jacob over which I tremble.
Therefore I will begin to pray and make supplication before you for myself and for them, because behold, I see the downfalls of us who dwell on the earth.
For I have also heard the decree of the judgment that is to come.
Therefore hear my voice, and listen to the words of my prayer, and I will speak before you, O Lord my God." The beginning of the words of the prayer of Ezra, which he prayed before he was taken up:
"O Lord, who dwell forever, whose heights are exalted and whose chambers are in the air,
he
whose throne
is boundless and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the heavenly hosts stand in fear;
he
at whose word
they are changed into fire and wind, whose word is faithful and whose utterance endures,
whose commandment is steadfast and whose decrees are terrible, whose look dries up the depths and whose indignation melts the mountains, whose truth bears witness:
Hear the voice of your servant, and listen to the supplication of your creature, and give heed to my words.
For as long as I live I will speak, and as long as I have understanding I will answer.
Do not look upon the sins of your people, but upon those who served you in truth.
And do not regard the foolish deeds of the ungodly, but those who kept your covenants in the midst of affliction.
And do not take thought of those who have conducted themselves wickedly before you, but remember those who willingly acknowledged the fear of you.
And do not desire to destroy those who have become like cattle, but look upon those who received the radiance of your law.
And do not be angry with those who have become worse than beasts, but love those who have continually placed their trust in your glory.
For we and those who were before us have done corrupt deeds and gone astray, but because of us sinners you are called merciful.
For if you desire to have mercy upon us who have no works of righteousness, then you will be named compassionate.
For the righteous, who have works laid up with you, shall receive their reward from their own deeds.
For what is a human being that you should be angry with him, or a corruptible race that you should be bitter against it?
For in truth, there is none among those born who has not done wickedness, and none among those who exist who has not sinned.
For by this your goodness is made known, O Lord, my Lord, when you have mercy upon those who have no strength of works."
And he answered and said to me, "Some things you have spoken correctly, and according to your words it shall be so.
For truly I will not consider the creation of the wicked, nor their death, nor their judgment, nor their destruction;
but I will rejoice over the coming of the creation of the righteous, and over their life, and over the payment of their reward.
For as I have spoken, so shall it be.
For just as a farmer sows many seeds and many plants
he plants,
yet not all the seeds live in due season, nor do all the plants take root, so also of those who have come into the world, not all shall be saved."
And I answered and said, "If I have found favor in your sight, let me speak before you.
For the seed of the farmer, if it does not receive your rain in its season, may not live, or it may be ruined by too much rain;
but a human being, who was fashioned by your hands and made in your image, for whose sake you created all things—have you likened him to the farmer's seed?"
No, I pray you, O Lord, my Lord, spare your people, and have mercy on your inheritance; for upon your creation
it is
indeed of your own that you have mercy.
And he answered and said to me, "The things of the present are for those of the present, and the things to come are for those who are to come."
For you fall far short of being able
to love
my creation
more than I. But you have compared yourself many times to the unrighteous. Never let it be so!
Yet even in this you will be praiseworthy before the Most High,
because you have humbled yourself, as becomes you, and have not ranked yourself among the righteous. Therefore, you will be greatly praised,
because many miseries will afflict the inhabitants of the world in the end, on account of the great pride with which they conducted themselves.
But understand concerning yourself, and seek out the glory of those who are like you.

For Paradise is opened for you, the tree of life is planted, the age to come is prepared, abundance is made ready, the city is built, rest is established, goodness is perfected, and wisdom is made complete.
The root is sealed off from you, illness is extinguished from you, and death is hidden; Sheol has fled, and corruption is forgotten;
and pains have departed from you, and in the end the treasures of life are revealed.
Therefore, do not ask any more questions concerning the multitude of those who perish,
for they received freedom, but they despised the Most High, greatly scorned his law, and abandoned his ways.
Moreover, they even trampled on his holy ones,
and said in their hearts that there is no God, though they well knew that they must die.
Therefore, just as the things previously mentioned await you, so also for them
thirst and torment
are prepared. For the Most High did not desire that human beings should perish;
but those who were created defiled the name of their Maker, and were ungrateful, and did not give thanks to me, who prepared life for them.
Therefore, my judgment is drawing near,
which I have not made known to many, but only to you and to the few who are like you." And I answered and said,
"Behold, Lord, now you have shown me a multitude of the signs that you will do in the last days, but you have not made known to me at what time."
And he answered and said to me, "Measure carefully within yourself; and when you see that a certain part of the signs mentioned beforehand has passed,
then understand that this is the very time in which the Most High will visit the world that was made by him.
And when there shall appear in the world earthquakes of places, turmoil of peoples, intrigues of nations, unrest among leaders, and the confusion of princes,
then understand that it was concerning these that the Most High spoke from of old.
For just as with everything that occurred in the world, its beginning is known and its end is manifest,
so also the times of the Most High: their beginnings are known by wonders, signs, and mighty acts, and their end by retribution and signs.
And it shall be that whoever shall be saved, and whoever shall be able to escape on account of his works or on account of his faith by which he believed,
he will survive the dangers mentioned beforehand, and will see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have consecrated for myself from eternity.
Then those who have now neglected my ways will be astonished, and those who despised and cast them away will abide in torments.
For all who did not acknowledge me in their life, even when they were receiving benefits from me,
and all who grew arrogant against my law while they still had freedom,
and while the opportunity for patience was still open to them, and they did not understand but neglected it—for these
it was necessary
that they should learn after death.
Therefore, do not inquire any longer how the ungodly are tormented, but seek how the righteous are saved, to whom the world belongs, and for whose sake the world was made."
And I answered and said,
"I say again now, and I will say it again hereafter: those who perish are more numerous than those who are saved,
even as the wave is greater than a drop."

And he answered and said to me, "As is the land, so also is its seed; and as are the flowers, so also are their colors; and as is the work, so also are the scents; and as is the farmer, so also is the threshing floor.
For there was a time of the world when I was preparing for those who now exist, before the worlds were made in which they should dwell; and no one opposed me, for indeed there was no one.
And now, though they have been created in a world that is prepared, and at a table that does not fail, and under an unsearchable law, they have become corrupted in their ways.
So I looked upon my world, and behold, it was ruined; and upon my inhabited earth, and behold, it was in peril, on account of the plots of its inhabitants.
And I saw and spared a very small remnant, and preserved for myself a single grape from a cluster, and a plant from a great forest.
Let the multitude perish, then, since it was made in vain; but let my grape and my plant be preserved, which were fashioned with much labor."
But as for you, if you set apart another seven days, yet you shall not fast in them again,
and go to the field of flowers where no house has been built, and eat only of the flowers of the field, and taste no meat, and drink no wine, but only the flowers;
and pray to the Most High continually, then I will come to you and speak with you."
So I went, as he commanded me, to the field which is called Arphad, and I sat there among the flowers of the ground, and I ate of the herbs of the field, and their nourishment satisfied me.
And it came to pass after seven days, while I was lying on the grass, my heart began again to be troubled within me, as before.
And my mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High, and I said:
"O Lord, my Lord, you were revealed to our fathers in the wilderness of Sinai, when they came out from Egypt, and when they were passing through the wilderness, in a land where there is no fruit,
and through which no
one passed; and you said to them:
'Hear me, O Israel, and listen to my words, O seed of Jacob!
For behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring forth in you the fruits of righteousness, and you shall be glorified in it forever.'

Yet our fathers received the law and did not keep it, and the commandments, and did not perform them. And the fruits of your law remained imperishable, for they could not perish, because they were yours.
Yet those who received it perished, because they did not keep that which had been sown in them.
And this is the law: when the earth receives seed, or the sea a ship, or any other vessel food that is placed in it, or whatever is deposited or kept,
when they are destroyed, the things that received them remain; but with us it was not so.
Rather, we who received the law and sinned perish along with our heart that received it.
Yet your law does not
perish,
but remains in its glory."

And while I was speaking these things in my heart, I lifted up my eyes and saw a woman on the right side, lamenting and weeping with a loud voice, and she was sighing deeply in her soul and grieving greatly; and her clothes were torn, and dust was cast upon her head.
Then I dismissed the thoughts that I had been thinking, and I turned to her and said to her,
"Why are you weeping, and why are you grieving in your soul?"
And she answered and said to me, "Leave me alone, my lord, that I may weep for myself and continue to sigh, for my soul is very bitter, and I am brought very low."
And I said to her, "Tell me what has happened to you." And she answered and said to me,
"I, your handmaid, was barren and did not give birth, though I was with my husband thirty years.
And every day and at every hour during these thirty years, I was praying and entreating the Most High, day and night.

And it came to pass after these thirty years, God heard the voice of your handmaid, and saw her humiliation, and looked upon my distress, and gave me a son. And I rejoiced and was delighted in him greatly, I and my husband and all the people of my city; and we glorified the Mighty One.
And I brought him up with great toil.
And when he grew up, I went to take a wife for him, and I made a wedding feast and a great banquet.
And it came to pass that when my son entered his wedding chamber, he fell down and died.
Then I overturned the lamps, and all the people of my city arose to comfort me; and I remained silent until the next day and until night.
And after they had all fallen asleep, thinking that I also was asleep, I arose in the night and fled, and came, as you see, to this field.
And I intend not to enter the city again, but to remain here, and neither eat nor drink, but continually mourn and fast until I die."
The woman whom you saw, this is Zion, whom you now see being built as a city.
Then I dismissed these thoughts that I had been thinking, and I answered in anger and said to her,
"You are the most foolish of all women! Do you not see our mourning and what has happened to us?
For behold, Zion, the mother of us all, is in great distress and is humbled with great humiliation.
Now it is right to mourn; we are all mourning. For you grieve for one son, but we, the whole world, for our mother.
Ask the earth, and she will tell you; for it is she that ought to mourn, because many are those who have come into being upon her.
And from the beginning, all who were upon her and others who are to come, behold, they all go to destruction, and their multitude is destined for corruption.
Who, then, ought to mourn more: she who has lost this whole multitude, or you, who mourn for one?
And if you should say to me, 'My mourning is not like that of the earth, for I
the fruit
of my womb have lost, which I bore in travail and brought up in pain;'
for the earth, according to the nature of the earth, the multitude departed which came to it just as it came—then I say to you again:
'Just as you bore in toil, so also the earth has given its fruit from the beginning, humankind, to him who made it.'
Now therefore, keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear with strength the misfortune that has befallen you.
For if you acknowledge the decree of the Most High to be just, you will also receive your son in time, and you will be praised among women.
Go, then, into the city to your husband." And she answered and said to me,
"I will not do so, and I will not enter the city, nor go to my husband, but here I will die."
And I continued further to speak with her, and said to her:
No, woman, no, woman! Do not do this thing; but be persuaded by the misfortune of Zion, and be comforted because of the pain of Jerusalem.
For behold, you have seen our sanctuaries that are desolated, and our altars that are overthrown, and our temple that is demolished,

and our service that has ceased, and our praise that has been taken away, and our boast that has fallen, and the light of our lampstand that is extinguished, and the ark of the covenant that has been plundered, and our holy things that are defiled, and the name that was called upon us that has been profaned, and our freeborn who have been dishonored, and our priests who have been burned with fire, and our Levites who have gone into captivity, and our virgins who have been defiled, and our wives who have been ravished by force, and our seers who have been snatched away,
and our righteous
have been scattered, and our young men have been enslaved, and our strong men have been made feeble.
And what is greater than all these is the seal of Zion, for the seal of her glory has now been taken away, and she has been delivered into the hands of those who hate us.
You, therefore, cast away from yourself the multitude of your pains, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you, and the Most High may give you rest from the pains of your toil.

And it happened that while I was speaking with her, behold, her face shone exceedingly, and the appearance of her countenance became like the likeness of lightning. And I was very afraid to approach her, and my heart was greatly astonished. And while I was wondering what this vision was,
suddenly she cried out with a loud and fearful voice, so that the whole earth shook at her voice.

And I looked, and behold, the woman was no longer visible to me, but a city that was being built, and a place was visible as with great foundations. And I was afraid, and I cried out with a loud voice and said:
"Where is Uriel the angel, who came to me from the first day? For he caused me to come into the multitude of this trembling, and my end has become destruction, and my prayer a reproach."
And while I was speaking these words, lying like a dead man upon the earth, the angel came to me, who had come to me before; and he saw me
lying upon the earth like a dead man, and my mind was confused. And he took me by my right hand, strengthened me, set me on my feet, and said to me:
"What is the matter with you? And why are you shaken? And why is your understanding disturbed, and the perception of your heart?" And I said to him:
"Because you have forsaken me. For I did as you told me, and
went out
into the field; and behold, I have seen and still see what I am unable to explain." And he answered and said to me:
"Stand upon your feet, and I will make it known to you." And I said to him:
"Speak, my lord; only do not forsake me, lest I die before my time.
For I have seen what I did not know, and I hear what I do not understand.
Or is my mind deceiving me, and my soul seeing a dream?
Now therefore I beg you, my lord, make known to your servant concerning this fearful vision."
And he answered and said to me: "Listen to me, and I will teach you, and reveal to you concerning the things of which you are afraid; because the Most High has revealed many mysteries to you.
For he has seen your uprightness, that you grieve greatly over your people, and mourn greatly over your people, and mourn greatly over Zion.
This, therefore, is the matter: The woman who appeared to you a little while ago,
who was mourning, and you began
to comfort her,
and who now no longer appears to you as a woman, but appeared to you as a city being built,
and who recounted to you concerning the misfortune of her son—this is the interpretation:
And as for her telling you concerning herself that she was barren for thirty years, it is because there were three thousand years in the world when no offering was offered in her.
And it happened after three thousand years that Solomon built the city and offered an offering in it; then it was that the barren woman bore a son.
And as for her telling you that she reared him
in the world, this
was the habitation of Jerusalem.
And as for her telling you, 'My son entered into his bridal chamber and died,' this was the downfall and misfortune of Jerusalem.
And as you saw her likeness, how she was mourning over her sons, and you began to comfort her concerning what had happened to her;
and now the Most High has seen that with all your soul you are grieving, and with all your heart you are pained over her; and he has shown you the light of the glory and the beauty
of her splendor.
For this reason I told you to wait for me in the field, where no house has been built.
For I knew that the Most High was going to show you all these things.
For this reason I told you to come to a place where there is no foundation of a building.
For no work of human hands could endure in a place where the city of the Most High was going to be revealed.
Therefore do not be afraid, and let not your heart be terrified; but go in and see the light of her glory and the greatness of her building, as much as the sight of your eyes is able to see.
And after these things you will hear as much as the hearing of your ears is able to hear.
For you are blessed beyond many, and have been named before the Most High as few are.
Tomorrow night, therefore, remain here,
and the Most High will show you the vision of revelations—those things which the Most High will do to the inhabitants of the earth in the last days."
And I slept there that night and the next, as he had commanded me.
And it happened on the second night that I saw a dream, and behold, an eagle was coming up from the sea, exceedingly great in its size; and it had twelve wings and three heads.
And I looked, and behold, it spread its wings over all the earth, and all the winds of heaven blew toward it, and the clouds gathered to it.
And I looked, and out of its wings were born small wings, slender and tiny.
Its heads, however, were at rest; the middle head was larger than the others, yet it too was at rest with them.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle commanded its wings to rule over all the earth and over its inhabitants.
And I saw how everything under heaven was made subject to it, and nothing resisted it among the creatures that are on the earth.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle stood up on its talons, and raised its voice to its wings, and said to them, “Go, rule over all the earth; but now rest,
and do not seek to awake all at once, but sleep, each one of you in his place, and awake in succession;
but let the heads be kept for the end.”
And I looked, and its voice did not come out from its heads, but from the midst of its body.
And I counted its small wings, and they were eight.
And I looked, and behold, one wing arose on the right side, and ruled over all the earth.
And I saw that its end came and it vanished, so that even its place was not known. And I looked, and behold, a second wing arose, and it too ruled over all the earth for a long time.
And it came to pass that when it was ruling, its end came to vanish like the first.
And behold, a voice was heard speaking to it, saying:
“Hear, you who have held the earth for all this time! Receive this announcement before you vanish:
None of those after you shall hold rule as long a time as this, nor even half of it.”
And I looked, and behold, the third wing arose, and it too ruled over all the earth like its previous companions; and it also vanished like the first ones.
And thus
it happened
to all the wings, that each one of them ruled, and again vanished.
And I looked, and behold, in time the small wings also arose on the right side, so that they might hold the earth; and some of them held rule, but quickly vanished.
And some of them arose, but did not hold dominion.
And after these things I looked, and its twelve wings had vanished, and two of the small wings.
And nothing remained of the body of the eagle, except only the three heads that were at rest, and six small wings.
And I looked, and behold, two wings separated from the small wings, and went and stood under the head that was on the right side; but four remained in their place.
And I looked, and behold, those four small wings planned to arise and seize dominion.
And I looked, and behold, one arose, but quickly vanished.
And again a second, but it too vanished quickly,
even more so than
the first.
And I looked, and behold, those two that remained of them were also planning to seize the headship.
And while they were planning to rule over the earth, I looked, and behold, one of the heads that were at rest—the middle one—awoke. It was larger than the two other heads,
[and joined] the two with it.
And together with the two that were with it, it turned and devoured the two small wings that were planning to rule.
Moreover, that head gained control over all the earth, and oppressed its inhabitants with great hardship, and held sway over the world more than all the wings that had been.
And after these things I looked, and behold, suddenly that middle head vanished, it too, just as
the wings.
And two heads remained, and they also ruled over all the earth and over its inhabitants.
And I looked, and behold, the head on the right side devoured the one on the left.
And I heard a voice saying to me, “Look straight before you, Ezra, and consider what you see at the end.”
And I looked, and behold, as it were a lion aroused from
the forest,
roaring and growling; and I heard how it uttered a human voice to the eagle, and spoke and said to it:
“Hear, you eagle, and I will speak to you; the Most High says to you:
‘Are you not the one that remains of the four beasts which I made to reign in my world, that the end of the times might come through them?’

‘And you, the fourth, came and overcame all the beasts that had passed, and you held sway over the world with great hardships, and over the whole earth with bitter oppression, and you dwelt in the world with deceit for a long time.’
‘And you have judged the earth without truth;’

‘for you have plundered and robbed the meek and faithful, and harmed the humble, and hated the upright, and loved liars, and destroyed the strongholds of those who were prosperous, and cast down the walls of those who did you no harm.’
‘And your insolence has reached the Most High, and your pride the Mighty One.’
‘And the Most High looked upon his times, and behold, they are ended, and his ages are completed.’”
Therefore you shall surely be destroyed, O eagle, you and your haughty wings, and your little, wicked wings, and your bitter heads, and your evil talons, and your whole hateful and wicked body,
so that the whole earth may be refreshed and relieved, once delivered from your violence, looking for the judgment and the mercies of its Maker.”
And it came to pass, while the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked,
and behold, the head that remained was suddenly destroyed; and then those two wings that went over to it arose to rule, and their rule was short and full of turmoil.
And I looked, and they too were destroyed, and the whole body of the eagle burned, and the earth was exceedingly terrified. But I awoke from great trembling and great fear, and I said to my spirit:
“You have brought all these things upon me, because you search out the ways of the Most High.
And behold, I am exhausted in my soul, and my spirit is very faint, and not even a little strength is left in me, because of the great fear with which I was terrified this night.
And now I will pray to the Most High, that he may strengthen me unto the end.”
And I said, “O Lord, my Lord, if I have found mercy in your sight, and if indeed I am blessed before you more than many, and if my prayer has truly ascended before the majesty of your presence,
strengthen me and make known to me, your servant, the interpretation and explanation of this vision that I saw, so that you may fully comfort my soul.
For you have judged me worthy, though I am not worthy, to reveal to me the end of times and the conclusion of the seasons.” And he answered and said to me:
“This is the interpretation of the vision that you saw:
The eagle that you saw coming up from the sea is the fourth kingdom that appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel.
But it was not explained to him as I now explain it to you, or as I have explained it to you.
Behold, the days are coming, and a kingdom shall arise on the earth, and it shall be more terrifying than all the kingdoms that were before it.
And twelve kings shall reign in it, one after another.
And the second, when he reigns, shall hold the time longer than any of the twelve.
This is the interpretation of the twelve wings that you saw.
And as for your seeing a voice speaking, and it did not come out from the heads of the eagle, but from the midst of its body,

this is the word: in the midst of the time of that kingdom there shall arise great divisions, and it shall be in danger of falling; yet it shall not fall then, but shall be established again in its former dominion.
And as for your seeing eight small wings growing under its wings,
this is the word: eight kings shall arise in it, whose times shall be short and their seasons swift; and two of them shall perish
when the middle time approaches; and four shall be kept for the time when its time approaches to end; but two shall be kept for the end.
And as for your seeing three heads resting on it,
this is the word: in the end of times the Most High will raise up three kings, and they shall renew many things in it, and crush the earth
and its inhabitants with great oppression, more than all those who were before them. Therefore, they are called the heads of the eagle,
for it is they who shall renew its wickedness and bring about its end.
And as for your seeing that one large head disappear, it means that one of them will die alone on his bed, and even he in torment.
But as for the two that remain, the sword shall devour them.
For the sword of the one shall devour
his fellow;
yet he also shall fall by the sword at the last.
And as for your seeing two wings going over to the head that is on the right side,
this is the word: these are they whom the Most High has kept for the end; and their kingdom shall be short and full of turmoil,
as you saw. And as for your seeing a lion roused from the forest, roaring and growling, and speaking to the eagle and rebuking it for its unrighteousness and all the words that you heard,

this is the Messiah whom the Most High has kept for the end of days, who shall arise from the seed of David; and he will come and speak to them, and rebuke them for their wickedness, and reprove them for their malice, and set their iniquity before them.
For he will set them alive before my judgment seat, and it will be that when he has rebuked them, then he will destroy them.

But he will deliver my remaining people with mercy, those who have remained within my borders, and he will gladden them until the end of the day of judgment comes, concerning which I spoke with you from the beginning.
This is the vision that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
And you alone were found worthy to know this secret of the Most High.
Write therefore in a book all these things that you have seen, and put them in a secret place;
and teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to hold and keep these secrets.
But as for you, wait here seven more days, so that whatever the Most High pleases to reveal to you may be revealed to you.”

And he departed from me. And it came to pass, when the people saw that seven days had passed and I had not returned to the city, all the people gathered together, from the least to the greatest, and they arose and came to me, and answered and said to me:
“How have we sinned against you, or how have we wronged you, that you have forsaken us and sat down in this place?
For of all the prophets you alone are left to us, like a cluster from the vintage, and like a lamp in a dark place, and like a haven of safety for a ship in a storm.
Are not the evils that have befallen us enough for us, that you also should forsake us?
For if you forsake us, it would have been better for us if we also had burned in the burning of Zion.
For we are not better than those who died there.” And they wept with a loud voice. And I answered and said to them:
“Take courage, O Israel, and do not grieve, O house of Jacob!
For your memorial is before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you forever.
As for me, I have not forsaken you, nor will I forsake you; but I came to this place to pray over the desolation of Zion, and to ask for mercy over the humiliation of our sanctuary.
And now go, each of you to his house, and I will come to you after these days.
So the people went into the city, as I told them.
But I sat in the field for seven days, as he commanded me; and I ate only of the flowers of the field, and from its roots was my nourishment in those days.
And it came to pass after seven days that I saw a vision in the night.
And behold, a great wind arose from the sea so as to stir up all its waves.

And I looked, and behold, that wind brought up from the heart of the sea as it were the likeness of a man. And I looked, and behold, that man was flying with the clouds of heaven; and wherever he turned his face to look and see, everything trembled before his sight.
And wherever the voice of his mouth went forth, all who heard his voice melted, just as wax melts when it feels the fire.
And I looked after these things, and behold, an innumerable multitude of people was gathered together from the four winds of heaven, to wage war against that man who came up from the sea.
And I saw that he carved out for himself a high mountain, and he flew and stood upon it.
But I sought to see the place or spot from which that mountain was carved out, and I could not.
And after these things I looked, and behold, all those who had gathered to wage war against him were very terrified; yet they dared to fight.
And when he saw the onslaught of the coming of their multitude as it approached, he did not raise his hand, nor did he hold a spear, nor any weapon of war; but I saw

how he sent forth from his mouth only as it were waves of fire, and from his lips a breath of flame, and from his tongue he shot out fiery coals of tempest; and all these mingled together—the waves of fire, the breath of flame, and the multitude of the tempest.

And they fell upon the oncoming rush of that great multitude which was prepared to fight, and burned them all up suddenly, so that nothing was seen of that innumerable multitude except only dust of ashes and the smell of smoke; and I looked and was astonished.
And after these things, I saw that man descending from that mountain, and calling to himself another multitude, a peaceful crowd.
And there drew near

to him the figures of many people; some of them were joyful, but some were grieving, and some were bound, and some were bringing those who were being offered. Then from the greatness of my fear I awoke, and I prayed to the Most High and said:
“You showed these wonders to your servant from the beginning, and though I am not worthy, you considered me deserving to receive my prayer.
And now reveal to me also the interpretation of this vision.
For as I consider in my mind, woe to those who are left behind in those days, and much more, woe to those who are not left behind!
For because they were not
left behind,
they shall grieve
over what is kept for those who are left behind in the last days, but they themselves do not reach them, as well as for those who are left behind.
On this account, woe! For they see great dangers with many tribulations, as these visions show.
Yet it is better for a man to endure danger and come to these things, than to pass away like a cloud from the world and not see what happens at the end of the times.”
And he answered and said to me, “I will tell you also the interpretation of your vision, and I will reveal to you concerning the things of which you have spoken.
Because you spoke of those who are left behind and of those who are not left behind, this is the explanation:
He who endures danger at that time, he keeps those
who fall into danger,
who have works and faith toward the Most High and the Mighty One.
Know, therefore, that blessedness is given to those who are left behind more than to those who have died.
Now this is the interpretation of your vision: Because you saw a man coming up from the heart of the sea,
he is the one whom the Most High has kept for many times, the one by whose hand he will deliver his creation; and he will guide those who are left behind.
And because you saw that from his mouth went forth a breath of fire and of tempest,
and that he was not holding a spear or any weapon of war in his hand, yet destroyed the onslaught of the coming of that host which came to wage war with him, this is the meaning:
Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will begin to deliver those who are upon the earth,
and great astonishment shall come upon the inhabitants of the earth.
And they shall plan to war against one another, city against city, region against region, nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And it shall come to pass, when these signs happen which I told you before, then my Son shall be revealed, whom you saw as a man coming up.
And when all the nations hear his voice, each of them shall leave his own region and their mutual warfare,
and an innumerable host shall be gathered together, as you saw, desiring to come and wage war against that man.
But he shall stand upon the summit of Mount Zion.
And Zion shall come and be revealed to all, prepared and built, just as you saw the mountain carved out without hands.

And my Son shall reprove for their ungodliness those nations that have come—those who were likened to a tempest—and shall set before them their evil deeds and the torment with which they are about to be tortured.
Then he who was likened to a flame shall destroy them without effort by means of the Law, which was likened to fire.
And because you saw him calling and gathering to himself another multitude, a peaceful crowd,

these are the nine and a half tribes that were taken captive from their land in the days of King Josiah, whom Shalmaneser the king of the Assyrians led captive, and brought them across the Euphrates River, and they were taken captive into another land.
For they took counsel among themselves and formed this plan, to leave the multitude of the nations and go to a more distant region, where the human race had never dwelt,
that there at least they might keep their law, which they had not kept in their own land.
And they entered by the narrow passages of the Euphrates.
For the Most High then performed wonders for them, and held back the channels of the river until they had all crossed over.
For through that region there was a great way to go, a journey of a year and a half; and that country is called Arzaph, at the end of the world.
And they lived there until the last time; and now when they are about to come again,
the Most High will again hold back the channels of the river Euphrates, so that they may be able to cross over. Therefore you saw a multitude gathered together in peace.
Moreover, those who are left of your people shall live, those who are found within my holy borders.
And it will come to pass, when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he will defend the people who are left.
And then he will show them very many wonders.”
And I said to him again, “O Lord, my Lord, explain this to me: why did I see the man coming up from the heart of the sea?” And he answered and said to me:
“Just as no one is able to explore and find out or know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one of those on earth is able to see my Son or those who are with him, except at that time in his day.
This is the interpretation of the vision that you saw. For this reason these things were revealed to you, to you alone,
because you have forsaken your own concerns and devoted yourself to those
that are mine,
and you have sought out those that belong to the Law.
For you have conducted your life in wisdom, and called understanding your mother.
Therefore I have shown you these things; for there is a reward with the Most High. And it will be after three days that I will speak other things to you, and explain to you other wonders.”
Then I went and walked extensively in the field, praising and giving thanks to the Most High for the wonders that he worked from time to time,
and because he governs the times and what comes in the times. And I remained there three days.
And it came to pass after these things, while I was sitting under an oak tree,
behold, a voice came out of a bush opposite me and spoke, saying to me, “Ezra, Ezra!” And I said, “Here I am,” and I stood up on my feet. And he said to me:
“I clearly revealed myself in a bush and spoke with Moses when my people were enslaved in Egypt;
and I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him to Mount Sinai, and kept him with me for many days;
and I explained to him many wondrous things, and made known to him the mysteries of the times, and showed him the end of the ages; and I commanded him, saying,
‘These words you shall conceal some of them, and some you shall make public.’
And now I say to you, Ezra:
The signs that I previously showed you, and the visions that you saw, and their interpretations that you heard—lay them up in your heart and hide them.
For you shall be taken away from humanity, and henceforth you shall be with my Son and with those who are like you, until the times are completed.
For the world has lost its youth, and the times are drawing near to grow old.
Now therefore, set your house in order, and reprove your people, and comfort their afflicted, and instruct their wise; and renounce now this corruptible life,

and loose from yourself the burden of humanity, and cast away the thoughts of death, and strip off now the nature of weakness, and set aside the thoughts that are burdensome to you, and hasten to depart from these times.
For evils worse than those which you have now seen happen will happen hereafter.
For the more the world weakens through its old age, the more evils will multiply upon the inhabitants of the earth.
For truth will withdraw even farther, and falsehood will draw near; for already the eagle which you saw in the vision is hastening to come.”
And I answered and said, “Let me speak before you, Lord.
Behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will reprove this present people; but for those who are yet to be born, who will warn them?
For the world lies in darkness, and its inhabitants are without light.
For your Law has been burned, and no one knows the works that you have done or what you are about to do.

If then I have found mercy before you, send the Holy Spirit into me, Lord, and I will write everything that has happened in the world from the beginning, all that was written in your Law, so that human beings may be able to find the path, and those who desire to live in the last days may know the way.”
And he answered and said to me, “Go and gather your people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.
But you, prepare for yourself
tablets
in great number, and take with you Seraiah, Daria, and Selemiah, together with Elkanah and Sheiel—these five men, because they are ready to write quickly;
and you shall come here, and I will light in your heart the lamp of understanding, which shall not be put out until what you are about to write is completed.
And when you have finished, some of them you shall make public, and some you shall conceal and deliver to the wise. For tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write.”
Then I went as he had commanded me, and gathered all the people, and said to them:
“Hear these words, O Israel!
Our ancestors were sojourners in ancient times in the land of Egypt, and they were delivered from there,
and they received the Law of life, but they did not keep it, which you also have transgressed after them.
And the land was given to you for an inheritance in the land of Zion; but you and your fathers did unrighteously and did not keep the ways which Moses commanded you,
the servant
of the Lord.
And the Most High, who is a righteous judge, took away from you that which had been given to you for a time.
And now you are here in distress, and your brothers are farther inside than you in another land.
If, therefore, you will rule over yourselves and discipline your heart, in your life you will be preserved, and after death mercy will be upon you.
For the judgment will come after death, when we live again; and then the name of the righteous will be revealed, and the deeds of the ungodly will be seen.
But let no one come near me, and do not seek me for forty days.
So I took these five men, just as he commanded me, and went to the field, and we remained there as he told me.
And it came to pass on the next day, behold, a voice called to me and said: "Ezra, Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink."
And I opened my mouth, and behold, there was offered to me a full cup; and it was full as of water, but its appearance was like fire.
And I took it and drank; and it came to pass while I was drinking it, behold, my heart poured forth understanding, and wisdom increased in my breast, and my spirit retained its memory.
And my mouth was opened, and was not closed again.

And the Most High gave understanding to those five men, and they wrote down what was spoken in order, in characters of signs which they did not know; and I sat there forty days. And they wrote by day,
and at night they ate bread only. But I spoke by day, and was not silent at night.
And in those forty days ninety-four books were written.

And it came to pass when the forty days were completed, the Most High spoke with me and said to me: "The twenty-four books that you have written first, place openly, and let the worthy and the unworthy among the people read them;
but keep these seventy, and deliver them to the wise of your people.
For in them are the veins of understanding, and the fountain of wisdom, and the light of knowledge."

ms.name: OCP Translation
ms.bibliography: English translation of Latin (English) based on the OCP critical edition.

unit.reading: In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city, I, Salathiel (who am also Ezra), was in Babylon. And I was troubled as I lay upon my bed, and my thoughts welled up in my heart,
because I saw the desolation of Zion and the wealth of those who lived in Babylon.
And my spirit was greatly agitated, and I began to speak words of fear to the Most High,
and I said: "O Sovereign Lord, did you not speak at the beginning, when you formed the earth—and that alone—and commanded the dust,
and it gave Adam a lifeless body? Yet it was the workmanship of your hands, and you breathed into him the breath of life, and he was made alive before you.
And you led him into paradise, which your right hand had planted before the earth appeared.

And to him you commanded one observance of yours, but he transgressed it, and immediately you appointed death for him and for his generations. And from him were born nations and tribes, peoples and clans, of which there is no number.
And every nation walked according to its own will, and they acted godlessly before you and despised your commandments, and you did not prevent them.
Then again, in due time, you brought the flood upon the inhabitants of the world and destroyed them.
And their fate was one: just as death came to Adam, so the flood came to these.
Yet you left one of them, Noah with his household, and from him all the righteous.
And it came to pass, when those who lived on the earth began to multiply, and produced children and peoples and many nations, they began again to practice godlessness more than the former ones.
And it came to pass, when they were committing iniquity before you, you chose for yourself one from among them, whose name was Abraham.
And you loved him, and to him alone you showed the end of the times secretly by night.
And you established an eternal covenant with him and told him that you would never forsake his descendants. And you gave him Isaac, and to Isaac you gave Jacob and Esau.
And you set Jacob apart for yourself, but Esau you put aside; and Jacob became a great multitude.
And it came to pass, when you led his descendants out of Egypt, you brought them to Mount Sinai.
You bent down the heavens and established the earth, and shook the world and made the deeps tremble, and threw the age into turmoil.
And your glory passed through four gates—of fire, and earthquake, and wind, and frost—to give the law to the seed of Jacob and the commandment to the generation of Israel.
Yet you did not take away from them their evil heart, that your law might bear fruit in them.
For the first Adam, burdened with an evil heart, transgressed and was overcome, as were all who were born of him.
Thus the weakness became permanent: the law was in the heart of the people along with the evil root; and what was good departed, and the evil remained.
And the times passed and the years were ended, and you raised up for yourself a servant named David.
And you told him to build a city for your name, and to offer oblations to you in it from what is yours.
And this was done for many years. But the inhabitants of the city went astray,
doing in all things just as Adam and all his generations had done; for they also possessed an evil heart.
And you handed your city over into the hands of your enemies.
And I said then in my heart: 'Are the deeds of those who inhabit Babylon any better, and is this why she rules over Zion?'
For when I came here, I saw impieties without number, and my soul has seen many sinners in this thirtieth year, and my heart failed me,
because I saw how you endure those who sin and have spared those who act godlessly, and have destroyed your people and preserved your enemies, and have not made known
anything to anyone as to how this way may be forsaken. Does Babylon do better than Zion,
or has any other nation known you besides Israel? Or what tribes have believed your covenants as Jacob has,
whose reward has not appeared, nor has their labor borne fruit? For I have traveled extensively among the nations, and I saw that they prosper and are unmindful of your commandments.
Now therefore, weigh our iniquities and those of the inhabitants of the world on a balance, and the turn of the scale will be found where it inclines.
Or when have the inhabitants of the earth not sinned in your sight? Or what nation has kept your commandments in such a way?
You may indeed find individual men who have kept your commandments by name, but nations you will not find."
Then the angel who had been sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered me
and said to me: "Your heart has utterly failed in this age, and do you think you can comprehend the way of the Most High?"
And I said: "Yes, my lord." And he answered me and said: "I have been sent to show you three ways and to set before you three parables.
If you can declare one of these to me, I also will show you the way you desire to see, and I will teach you why the heart is evil."
And I said: "Speak, my lord." And he said to me: "Go, weigh for me the weight of fire, or measure for me the blast of the wind, or call back for me the day that has passed."
And I answered and said: "Who among mortals can do this, that you should ask me about these things?"

And he said to me: "If I had asked you, saying: 'How many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs are at the source of the deep, or how many streams are above the firmament, or what are the exits of paradise?'
perhaps you would have said to me: 'I have not descended into the deep, nor into Hades yet, nor have I ever ascended into heaven.'
But now I have not asked you except about fire and wind and the day through which you have passed—things from which you cannot be separated—and you have not answered me about them."
And he said to me: "You cannot understand the things that are your own, which have grown up with you;
how then can your vessel comprehend the way of the Most High? ... And how can one already worn out by a corrupt world understand incorruption?" And when I heard these things, I fell upon my face
and said to him: "It would be better for us not to be here than to come and live in ungodliness, and suffer, and not understand why."
And he answered me and said: "I went forth to the trees of the forest of the plain, and they took counsel
and said: 'Come, let us go and wage war against the sea, that it may recede before us, and that we may make for ourselves other forests.'"
And in like manner the waves of the sea also devised a plan and said, 'Come, let us go up and conquer the forest of the plain, so that there also we may make for ourselves another region.'
And the plan of the forest was in vain, for fire came and consumed it.
Likewise also the plan of the waves of the sea, for the sand stood firm and stopped them.
For if you were a judge of these, whom would you begin to justify, or whom to condemn?
And I answered and said, 'Both devised a vain plan, for the land was given to the forest, and the sea's place to bear its waves.'
And he answered me and said, 'You have judged well; why then have you not judged for yourself?'

For just as the land was given to the forest and the sea to its waves, so also those who dwell upon the earth can understand only what is upon the earth, and those who are above the heavens what is in the height of the heavens.
And I answered and said, 'I beseech you, Lord, why then was understanding given to me?'

For I did not wish to inquire about the higher ways, but about those things that pass through us daily: why Israel has been given over to the nations as a reproach, why the people whom you loved has been given to godless tribes, and the law of our fathers has been brought to destruction, and the written covenants are nowhere to be found.
And we pass away from the world like locusts, and our life is like a mist, and we are not worthy to obtain mercy.
But what will he do for his name which has been invoked over us? Concerning these things I asked.
And he answered me and said, 'If you exist you will see, and if you live you will marvel often, because the age is hastening swiftly to pass away.'
For it is not able to bear what has been promised for the righteous in their times, because this age is full of sorrow and infirmities.
For evil has been sown, concerning which you ask me, and its harvesting has not yet come.
If therefore that which was sown is not reaped, and the place where evil was sown does not pass away, the field where the good is sown will not come.
For a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness it has produced until now, and will produce until the threshing floor comes!
Consider now for yourself how much fruit of ungodliness a grain of evil seed has produced.
When countless ears of grain are sown, how great a threshing floor they will begin to make!
And I answered and said, 'How and when will these things be? Why are our years so few and evil?'
And he answered me and said, 'Do not hasten in spirit above the Most High; for you hasten on account of your own self, but the Most High on behalf of many.'
Did not the souls of the righteous in their chambers ask concerning these things, saying, 'How long must I hope like this? And when does the fruit of the harvest of our reward come?'
And Jeremiel the archangel answered them and said, 'When the number of those like you is completed; for he has weighed the age in the balance,
and with a measure he has measured the times, and by number he has numbered the times, and he will not move nor awaken them until the prescribed measure is fulfilled.'
And I answered and said, 'O Sovereign Lord, but we also are all full of ungodliness.'
'And perhaps on our account the harvest of the righteous is hindered, because of the sins of those who inhabit the earth.'
And he answered me and said, 'Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when she has completed her nine months, her womb can still retain the fetus within itself.'
And I said, 'It cannot, my lord.' And he said to me, 'In the underworld the chambers of souls are like the womb.'
For just as a woman in labor hastens to escape the anguish of childbirth, so also these hasten to give back what has been entrusted to them
from the beginning. Then it will be shown to you concerning the things you desire to see.'
And I answered and said, 'If I have found favor before your eyes, and if it is possible, and if I am worthy,
show me this also: whether more than what has passed is yet to come, or whether more has passed by us;
for what has passed I know, but what is to come I do not know.'
And he said to me, 'Stand on the right side, and I will show you the interpretation of the parable.'
And I stood and looked, and behold, a burning furnace passed before me; and it happened that when the flame had passed, I looked, and behold, smoke remained.
And after this a cloud full of water passed before me and poured out a great downpour of rain with violence; and when the violence of the rain had passed, drops remained in it.
And he said to me, 'Consider for yourself: just as the downpour exceeds the drops, and the fire exceeds the smoke, so the measure that has passed was far greater, while the drops and smoke remain.'
And I prayed and said, 'Do you think I shall live until those days? Or who will be alive in those days?'
He answered me and said, 'Concerning the signs about which you ask me, I can tell you in part; but concerning your life, I was not sent to tell you, for I do not know.'

'Now concerning the signs: behold, the days will come when those who dwell upon the earth shall be seized with great panic, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.
And unrighteousness shall be multiplied beyond that which you yourself see and beyond that which you heard of long ago.
And the land that you now see ruling shall be chaotic, without a footprint, and they shall see it desolate.
But if the Most High grants you to live, you shall see it thrown into confusion after the third trumpet, and the sun shall suddenly shine by night and the moon by day.
And blood shall drip from wood, and the stone shall utter its voice; and the peoples shall be thrown into commotion,
and the courses of the stars shall be altered. And one whom those who inhabit the earth do not expect shall reign, and birds shall migrate together.
And the Sea of Sodom shall cast up fish; and one whom many do not know shall utter a voice by night, but all shall hear its voice.
And chasms shall open in many places, and fire shall burst forth repeatedly, and wild beasts shall migrate beyond their territory, and menstruous women shall bring forth monsters;
and salt waters shall be found in the sweet. And all friends shall war against one another; and understanding shall then hide itself, and insight shall withdraw into its chamber.
And it shall be sought by many and not found, and unrighteousness and lack of restraint shall be multiplied upon the earth.
And one region will ask its neighbor, saying, 'Has righteousness, doing what is right, passed through you?' And it will say, 'No.'
And at that time it shall be that people will hope and not obtain; they will labor, but their ways will not prosper.'
I am permitted to tell you these signs; and if you pray again and weep as you do now, and fast for seven days, you shall hear yet greater things than these.
Then I awoke, and my body shuddered violently, and my soul was so troubled that it fainted.
And the angel who had come to speak with me took hold of me, strengthened me, and set me on my feet.
And it came to pass on the second night that Phalthiel, the leader of the people, came to me and said to me, "Where were you, and why is your face so sad?
Or do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the land of their exile?
Rise up therefore and eat some bread, and do not forsake us, like a shepherd who leaves his flock in the hands of wicked wolves."
And I said to him, "Go away from me and do not come near me for seven days, and then you may come to me." And he listened to what I said and departed from me.
And I fasted for seven days, wailing and weeping, just as the angel Uriel had commanded me.
And it came to pass after seven days that the thoughts of my heart were again very grievous to me.
Then my soul recovered the spirit of understanding, and I began once more to speak words before the Most High,
and I said: "O Sovereign Lord, from all the forests of the earth and from all its trees you have chosen for yourself one vine,
and from all the lands of the world you have chosen for yourself one plot, and from all the flowers of the world you have chosen for yourself one lily,
and from all the depths of the sea you have filled for yourself one river, and from all the built cities you have consecrated Zion for yourself,
and from all created birds you have named for yourself one dove, and from all the fashioned cattle you have provided for yourself one sheep,
and from all the multitudes of peoples you have acquired for yourself one people, and to this people, whom you desired, you gave the law approved by all.
And now, O Lord, why have you handed over the one to the many, and set the one root above the others, and scattered your only one among the many?
And those who opposed your promises have trampled upon those who believed your covenants.
And if you truly hate your people, they ought to be punished by your own hands."
And it came to pass, when I had spoken these words, that the angel who had previously come to me on the past night was sent to me,
and he said to me: "Listen to me, and I will instruct you; pay attention to me, and I will say more before you."
And I said, "Speak, my lord." And he said to me, "You are greatly distraught in mind concerning Israel; or do you love him more than he who made him?"
And I said, "No, lord, but I spoke in sorrow; for my kidneys torment me every hour as I seek to grasp the path of the Most High and to search out a part of his judgment."

And he said to me, "You cannot." And I said, "Why, lord? Why then was I born? Or why did not my mother's womb become my grave, so that I might not see the travail of Jacob and the exhaustion of the race of Israel?"
And he said to me, "Count for me those who have not yet come, and gather for me the scattered drops, and make the withered flowers green again for me,
and open for me the closed storehouses and bring out for me the winds shut up in them, or show me the likeness of a voice; and then I will show you the travail that you ask to see."
And I said, "O Sovereign Lord, who is able to know these things except one whose dwelling is not with mortals?
As for me, I am foolish; how then can I speak of these things about which you have questioned me?"
And he said to me, "Just as you cannot do one of these things that have been mentioned, so you will not be able to discover my judgment, or the goal of the love that I have promised for my people."
And I said, "Yet behold, Lord, you have charge of those who are at the end; but what will they do who were before me, or we ourselves, or those who come after us?"
And he said to me, "I will liken my judgment to a circle: just as there is no slowness of the last, so there is no swiftness of the first."
And I answered and said, "Could you not have made those who have been, and those who are, and those who are yet to be, all at once, so that you might show your judgment more quickly?"
And he answered me and said, "The creation cannot move faster than the Creator, nor can the world sustain all at once those who are created in it."

And I said, "How then did you say to your servant that you will give life all at once to the creation created by you? If therefore they shall live together and the creation can sustain them, it could also now bear them present all at once."
And he said to me, "Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her: 'If you bear ten children, why do you do so over time?' Ask her therefore to bring forth ten all at once."
And I said, "She certainly cannot, but only according to time."
And he said to me, "And I have given the womb of the earth to those who are sown upon it over time.
For just as an infant does not give birth, nor one who has grown old any longer, so have I ordered the world created by me."
And I questioned him and said, "Since you have now opened the way for me, let me speak before you: is our mother, of whom you spoke to me, still young, or is she now approaching old age?"
And he answered me and said, "Ask a woman who gives birth, and she will tell you.
For you will say to her: 'Why are those whom you have now borne not like those who were before them, but smaller in stature?'
And she herself will tell you: 'Those who were born in the youth of strength are of one sort, and those born at the time of old age, when the womb is failing, are of another.'
Consider therefore you also, that you are smaller in stature than those who were before you,

and those who come after you will be smaller than you, as of a creation already growing old and passing the strength of youth." And I said, "I beseech you, Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, show your servant through whom you visit your creation."
And he said to me: "At the beginning of the terrestrial world, before the portals of the world stood in place, and before the gatherings of the winds blew,
and before the sounds of the thunders resounded, and before the flashes of the lightnings shone, and before the foundations of paradise were laid,
and before the fair flowers were seen, and before the powers of movement were established, and before the innumerable hosts of angels were gathered,
and before the heights of the air were lifted up, and before the measures of the firmaments were named, and before the footstool of Zion was weighed,
and before the present years were searched out, and before the schemes of those who now sin were rejected, and before those who stored up faith were sealed—
then I planned these things, and they were made through me alone and not through another, just as the end also shall come through me and not through another."
Then I answered and said, "What will be the division of the times, or when will be the end of the first and the beginning of the next?"
And he said to me: "From Abraham to Abraham, because Jacob and Esau were born from him; for Jacob's hand held Esau's heel from the beginning.
For Esau is the end of this age, and Jacob is the beginning of the one that follows.
For the end of a man is the heel, and the beginning of a man is the hand; seek nothing else between the heel and the hand, Ezra."
And I answered and said: "O Sovereign Lord, if I have found favor in your sight,
show your servant the end of your signs, part of which you showed me on the preceding night."
And he answered and said to me: "Stand up on your feet, and you will hear a voice full of sound.
And it shall be that if the place where you stand is violently shaken,
when it speaks, do not be terrified, for the word concerns the end. And the foundations of the earth will understand
that the speech is about them; it will tremble and be shaken, for it knows that their end must be changed."
And it came to pass when I had heard this, I stood up on my feet and listened; and behold, a voice was speaking, and its sound was like the sound of many waters.
And it said: "Behold, the days are coming, and it shall be that when I begin to draw near to visit those who inhabit the earth,
and when I begin to make inquiry of those who have unrighteously harmed by their iniquity, and when the humiliation of Zion is fulfilled,
and when the age that is beginning to pass away is sealed, I will perform these signs: The books will be opened before the face of the firmament, and all will see together.
And one-year-old infants will speak with their voices, and pregnant women will give birth to premature infants of three and four months, and they will live and leap about.
And suddenly sown places will appear unsown, and full storehouses will suddenly be found empty;
and the trumpet will sound with a blast, and when all hear it, they will suddenly be terrified.

And it shall be at that time that friends will make war on friends as enemies, and the earth will be terrified along with those who inhabit it, and the springs of the fountains will stand still so that they do not flow for three hours.
And it shall be that everyone who is left of all these things that I have foretold to you will be saved, and will see my salvation and the end of my age.
And they will see the men who have been taken up, who have not tasted death from their birth, and the heart of the inhabitants will be changed and converted into another mind.
For evil will be blotted out, and deceit will be extinguished.
Faith will flourish, and corruption will be overcome, and the truth will be revealed, which has been without fruit for so long."
And it came to pass while he was speaking to me, behold, little by little the place upon which I was standing began to shake.
And he said to me: "I came to show you these things during the coming night.
If, therefore, you pray again and fast again for seven days, I will again announce to you greater things than these by day."
"For your voice has surely been heard before the Most High; for the Mighty One has seen your uprightness and has observed the purity which you have maintained from your youth.
And on this account he sent me to show you all these things and to say to you: 'Trust and do not be afraid,
and do not be in a hurry to ponder vain thoughts regarding the former times, so that you may not hasten from the last times.'"
And it came to pass after this that I wept again and likewise fasted seven days, so that I might complete the three weeks that were told to me.
And it came to pass on the eighth night that my heart was once again troubled within me, and I began to speak before the Most High.
For my spirit was greatly inflamed, and my soul was in distress.
And I said: "O Lord, you indeed spoke from the beginning of creation on the first day, saying: 'Let heaven and earth be made,' and your word accomplished the work.
And then the Spirit was hovering, and darkness was circling round about and silence; the sound of a human voice was not yet from you.
Then you commanded that a shining light be brought forth from your storehouses, so that your works might then appear.

And on the second day you created the spirit of the firmament and commanded it to divide and make a separation between the waters, so that one part might recede upward and the other part remain below.

And on the third day you commanded the waters to be gathered into the seventh part of the earth, but six parts you dried up and preserved, so that from these there might be fields sown and cultivated serving before you.
For your word went forth, and immediately the work was done.

For suddenly fruit of immense abundance went forth, and varied delight for the taste, and flowers of inimitable color, and scents of unsearchable fragrance. And these things were done on the third day.
On the fourth day you commanded the brightness of the sun to be made, the light of the moon, and the arrangement of the stars,
and you commanded them to serve man, who was to be formed.
On the fifth day you said to the seventh part where the water was gathered together, that it should produce living creatures, birds, and fish; and so it was done.
The mute and lifeless water, doing what it was commanded, produced living creatures, so that from this the nations might recount your wondrous works.
And then you preserved two living beings; the name of one you called Behemoth, and the name of the second you called Leviathan.
And you separated them from one another, for the seventh part where the water was gathered could not contain them.
And to Behemoth you gave one part which was dried up on the third day, that he might dwell in it, where there are a thousand mountains.
But to Leviathan you gave the seventh, watery part. And you have kept them to be devoured by whom you wish and when you wish.
On the sixth day you commanded the earth to create before you cattle, beasts, and creeping things;
and over these you placed Adam as ruler over all the works that you had made, and from him all of us are descended, the people whom you have chosen.
All these things I have spoken before you, O Lord, because you said that you created the firstborn world for our sake.
As for the remaining nations born of Adam, you said that they are nothing, and that they are likened to spittle, and you have compared their abundance to a drop from a bucket.
And now, O Lord, behold, these nations which are accounted as nothing rule over us and devour us."
But we, your people, whom you have called your firstborn, your only-begotten, your zealous lover, your most beloved, have been handed over into their hands.
And if the world was created for us, why do we not possess our world as an inheritance? How long will this endure?
And it came to pass, when I had finished speaking these words, that the angel who had been sent to me during the former nights was sent to me,
and he said to me: "Rise, Ezra, and hear the words that I have come to speak to you."
And I said: "Speak, my lord." And he said to me: "A sea is set in a wide expanse, so that it is deep and boundless;
but its entrance is set in a narrow place, so as to be like a river.
For if someone truly desires to go into the sea, to look upon it or to master it, how will he be able to reach the broad expanse unless he passes through the narrow part?
Again, another example: A city is built and set on a plain, and it is full of all good things;
but its entrance is narrow and set upon a precipice, so that there is fire on the right hand, and deep water on the left.
There is only a single path set between them, that is, between the fire and the water, so narrow that it can hold only one man's footstep at a time.
If now that city is given to a man as an inheritance, unless the heir passes through the danger set before it, how will he receive his inheritance?"
And I said: "So it is, lord." And he said to me: "So also is the portion of Israel.
For I made the world for their sake; and when Adam transgressed my statutes, what had been made was judged.
And the entrances of this world became narrow and sorrowful and toilsome, few and evil, full of perils and sustained by great hardships.
For the entrances of the greater world are spacious and secure, and yield the fruit of immortality.
Therefore, unless the living enter into these narrow and futile conditions, they will never be able to receive the things that are stored up.
Why then are you troubled, since you are corruptible? And why are you agitated, since you are mortal?
And why have you not considered in your heart what is to come, but only what is present?"
Then I answered and said: "O Sovereign Lord, behold, you have ordained in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the ungodly shall perish.
The righteous, therefore, endure narrow things while hoping for wide things; but those who have acted wickedly have suffered the narrow things and yet will not see the wide."
And he said to me: "You are not a judge above God, nor have you understanding above the Most High.
For let many of the present perish rather than that the law of God which was set before them be disregarded.
For the Lord strictly commanded those who came into the world when they came, what they should do to live, and what they should observe so as not to be punished.
Yet they were not convinced and spoke against him, and devised for themselves vain thoughts,
and planned deceitful sins for themselves; they even said that the Most High does not exist, and they did not know his ways.
And they despised his law, and rejected his covenants, and had no faith in his statutes, and did not perform his works.
Therefore, Ezra, empty things are for the empty, and full things are for the full.
For behold, the time will come, when the signs that I told you beforehand will come to pass, and the bride shall appear, even the city appearing, and the land that is now hidden shall be shown.
And everyone who has been delivered from the aforementioned evils shall see my wonders.
For my Son Jesus shall be revealed with those who are with him, and he shall rejoice those who remain for four hundred years.
And it will come to pass after these years, that my Son Christ shall die, and all who have human breath.
And the world shall be turned back into primeval silence for seven days, as it was in the first beginnings, so that no one shall be left.
And it will come to pass after seven days, that the world which is not yet awake shall be aroused, and the corruptible world shall die.
And the earth shall give up those who sleep in it, and the dust those who dwell silently in it, and the storehouses shall give up the souls that were entrusted to them.
And the Most High shall be revealed upon the judgment seat, and compassion shall pass away, and patience shall be withdrawn;
but judgment alone shall remain. Truth shall stand, and faithfulness shall grow strong;
and the deed shall follow, and the reward shall be shown; righteous deeds shall awake, and unrighteous deeds shall not sleep.
And the pit of torment shall appear, and opposite it shall be the place of rest; the furnace of Gehenna shall be shown, and opposite it the paradise of delight.
And the Most High will then say to the raised nations: 'Look and understand whom you have denied, or whom you have not served, or whose commandments you have despised.
Look on this side and on that: here is delight and rest, and there is fire and torment.' These things he shall speak to them on the day of judgment.
This is a day that has neither sun nor moon nor stars,
nor cloud nor thunder nor lightning, nor wind nor water nor air, nor darkness nor evening nor morning,
nor summer nor spring nor heat, nor winter nor frost nor cold, nor hail nor rain nor dew,
nor noon nor night nor dawn, nor brightness nor clarity nor light, except only the splendor of the glory of the Most High, by which all shall begin to see what is set before them.
For it will have a duration like a week of years.
This is my judgment and its ordinance; and to you alone have I shown these things."
And I answered and said then, O Lord, and I say now: "Blessed are those who are present and observe what has been established by you.
But concerning those for whom my prayer was made: who among the living has not sinned, or who of those born has not broken your covenant?
And now I see that the world to come will bring delight to few, but torments to many.

For an evil heart has grown up in us, which has alienated us from these things and led us into corruption, and showed us the paths of death and pointed out to us the ways of ruin, putting us far from life—and that, not just a few, but almost all who were created."
And he answered me and said, "Listen to me, and I will instruct you, and I will admonish you concerning what follows.
For this reason the Most High has not made one age, but two.
For because you have said that the righteous are not many but few, while the ungodly are multiplied, listen to this:
If you have very few precious stones, will you set them for yourself according to their number, while lead and clay are abundant?"
And I said, "Lord, how could that be?"
And he said to me, "Not only this, but ask the earth, and it will tell you; flatter it, and it will declare to you.
For you shall say to it: 'You produce gold and silver and bronze, and iron also, and lead and clay;
but silver is more abundant than gold, and bronze than silver, and iron than bronze, lead than iron, and clay than lead.'
