Judge therefore for yourself which things are precious and desirable: that which is abundant, or that which is born rare?"
And I said, "O Sovereign Lord, what is abundant is cheaper, for that which is rarer is more precious."
And he answered me and said, "Weigh within yourself what you have thought, for he who has what is difficult to obtain rejoices more than he who has an abundance.
So also is the creation promised by me. For I will rejoice over the few who are saved, because it is they who have now made my glory prevail, and through whom my name is now praised.
And I will not grieve over the multitude of those who perish, for they are the ones who are now like vapor, and are counted as flame and smoke; they burned and glowed, and are extinguished."
And I answered and said, "O earth, what have you brought forth! If mind is made from dust like the rest of creation,
it would have been better if the dust itself had not come into being, so that mind might not have been made from it.
For now the mind grows with us, and on this account we are tormented, because we perish while knowing it.
Let the human race mourn, and let the wild beasts rejoice; let all who are born lament, but let the four-footed beasts and cattle be glad!
For it is much better for them than for us, for they do not expect judgment, nor do they know torment or salvation promised to them after death.
For what does it profit us that we are to be saved, yet will be tormented with torment?
For all who have been born are entangled in iniquities, and full of sins, and burdened with transgressions.
And if we were not coming into judgment after death, perhaps it would have gone better for us."
And he answered me and said, "When the Most High was making the world and Adam and all who came from him, he first prepared the judgment and the things that belong to the judgment.
And now understand from your own words, for you said that the mind grows with us.

Therefore, those who dwell on the earth will be tormented for this reason: that having understanding they committed iniquity, and receiving the commandments they did not keep them, and having obtained the law they dealt deceitfully with what they had received.
And what will they have to say at the judgment, or how will they answer in the last times?
For how long a time the Most High has been patient with those who inhabit the world—and not for their sake, but for the sake of the times that he foresaw!"

And I answered and said, "If I have found favor before you, Lord, show this also to your servant: whether after death, or now when each one of us gives up his soul, we will be kept in rest until those times come in which you will begin to renew creation, or whether we will be tormented from now on?"
And he answered me and said, "I will show you this also. But do not join yourself with those who have shown contempt, nor count yourself among those who are tormented.
For indeed you have a treasure of works laid up with the Most High, but it will not be shown to you until the last times.

Now concerning death, the word is: When the decree has gone forth from the Most High that a person must die, as the spirit leaves the body to be returned again to him who gave it, first of all to worship the glory of the Most High:
if indeed it is of those who have shown contempt and have not kept the way of the Most High, and of those who have despised his law and hated those who fear God,
such spirits will not enter into habitations, but will wander about from then on in torments, always grieving and sorrowful, in seven ways.
The first way: because they have despised the law of the Most High.
The second way: because they can no longer make a good return, that they may live.
The third way: they see the reward laid up for those who have believed the covenants of the Most High.
The fourth way: they will consider the torment laid up for themselves in the last times.
The fifth way: seeing the habitations of others guarded by angels in great silence.
The sixth way: seeing how torment passes over them.

The seventh way, which is greater than all the aforesaid ways: because they will pine away in confusion and be consumed with shame and waste away in fear, seeing the glory of the Most High, before whom they sinned while living and before whom they are about to be judged in the last times.
Now this is the order of those who have kept the ways of the Most High, when they begin to be separated from the corruptible vessel:
In the time when they dwelt in it they served the Most High with toil, and endured danger at every hour, so that they might perfectly keep the law of the Lawgiver.
Therefore this is the word concerning them:
First of all, they see with great exultation the glory of him who receives them, for they will rest in seven orders.
The first order: because they strived with much toil to conquer the evil thought formed with them, so that it might not seduce them from life to death.
The second order: because they see the perplexity in which the souls of the ungodly wander, and the punishment that awaits them.
The third order: they see the testimony that he who formed them bore concerning them, because while living they kept the law that was given through faith.
The fourth order: they understand the rest which, now gathered in their chambers, they enjoy in great silence guarded by angels, and the glory that awaits them in their last times.

The fifth order: they exult over how they have now escaped the corruptible, and how they will possess the future as an inheritance, moreover seeing the narrow and toil-filled state from which they have already been delivered, and begin to receive the spacious room, rejoicing and immortal.
The sixth order: when it is shown to them how their face will begin to shine like the sun, and how they will begin to be made like the light of the stars, incorruptible from then on.

The seventh order, which is greater than all the aforesaid: because they will exult with confidence, and because they will trust without being confused, and will rejoice without fear; for they hasten to see the face of him whom they served while living and from whom they are to receive their reward in glory."
This is the order of the souls of the righteous, as it is announced henceforth; and these are the previously mentioned ways of torment which those who have been negligent will suffer henceforth.
And I answered and said, "Will time therefore be given to the souls, after they are separated from the bodies, that they may see that of which you have spoken to me?"
And he said to me, "Their freedom will be for seven days, so that during the seven days they may see the matters that have been foretold, and afterward they will be gathered into their habitations."

And I answered and said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, show further to me, your servant, whether on the day of judgment the righteous will be able to intercede for the ungodly or to entreat the Most High on their behalf,"
"whether fathers for sons, or sons for parents, or brothers for brothers, or kinsfolk for their nearest kin, or trusted friends for their dearest ones."

And he answered me and said, "Since you have found favor before my eyes, I will show this also to you. The day of judgment is decisive and displays to all the seal of truth. Just as now a father does not send his son, or a son his father, or a master his slave, or a trusted friend his dearest, that he may understand or sleep or eat or be healed for him,"
"so no one will ever pray for another; for all will then bear each his own unrighteousness or righteousness."
And I answered and said, "How then do we find that first Abraham prayed for the people of Sodom, and Moses for the fathers who sinned in the wilderness,"
"and Joshua after him for Israel in the days of Achan, and Samuel in the days of Saul,"
"and David for the plague, and Solomon for those in the sanctuary,"
"and Elijah for those who received the rain, and for the dead that he might live,"
"and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many for many?"
"If therefore now, when the corruptible has grown and unrighteousness has multiplied, the righteous have prayed for the ungodly, why will it not be so then also?"
And he answered me and said, "The present age is not the end; glory does not abide in it continuously; therefore those who were able prayed for the weak."
"For the day of judgment will be the end of this age and the beginning of the immortal age to come, in which corruption has passed away,"
"intemperance is dissolved, unbelief is cut off, but righteousness has grown, and truth has arisen."
"Therefore no one will then be able to have mercy on him who has been defeated in judgment, nor to harm him who has conquered."
And I answered and said, "This is my first and last word: it would have been better that the earth had not been given to Adam, or, when it had been given, to restrain him so that he would not sin."
"For what good is it to all to live in sorrow in the present and to expect punishment when dead?"
"O Adam, what have you done? For if you sinned, your fall was not yours alone, but ours also who are descended from you."
"For what good is it to us if an immortal age is promised to us, but we have done mortal deeds?"
"And that an everlasting hope has been foretold to us, but we have utterly become vain?"
"And that habitations of health and safety have been reserved, but we have lived wickedly?"
"And that the glory of the Most High is to protect those who have lived purely, but we have walked in the worst of ways?"
"And that paradise will be revealed, whose fruit endures incorruptible, in which is abundance and healing,"
"but we shall not enter it, for we have lived in unlovely places?"
"And that the faces of those who practiced self-restraint will shine brighter than the stars, but our faces will be blacker than darkness?"
"For while we lived and committed iniquity, we did not consider what we would suffer after death."
And he answered and said, "This is the meaning of the contest which the human being born on earth fights:"
"that if he is defeated, he will suffer what you have said, but if he conquers, he will receive what I say."
"For this is the way of which Moses spoke while he was alive, saying to the people: 'Choose life for yourself, that you may live.'"
"Yet they did not believe him, nor the prophets after him, nor even me who have spoken to them,"
"so that there should not be grief over their destruction, just as there will be joy over those for whom salvation is assured."
And I answered and said, "I know, Lord, that the Most High is now called merciful, in that he has mercy on those who have not yet entered into the world,"
"and compassionate, in that he has compassion on those who turn to his law,"
"and patient, because he shows patience to those who have sinned, as being his own works,"
"and bountiful, because he is willing to give rather than to demand,"
"and of great mercy, because he multiplies mercies all the more to those who are present, and to those who have passed away, and to those who are to come."
"For if he did not multiply them, the world with those who inhabit it would not remain alive."
"And a giver, for if he did not give out of his goodness, so that those who have committed iniquities might be relieved of their iniquities, not one ten-thousandth part of humankind could have life;"
"and a judge, for if he did not pardon those who were created by his word and blot out the multitude of their offenses, perhaps out of an innumerable multitude there would be left only very few."
And he answered me and said, "The Most High made this age for the sake of many, but the age to come for the sake of few."

"I will tell a parable before you, Ezra. Just as you might ask the earth, and it will tell you that it yields far more clay from which earthenware is made, but only a little dust from which gold comes, so also is the course of the present age."
"Many indeed are created, but few will be saved."
And I answered and said, "Therefore, O soul, absorb understanding and devour what is wise!"
"For you have come without your consent and you depart against your will; for no span has been given to you except only to live a short time."

"O Lord above us, if you will permit your servant that we may pray before you, grant to us the seed of the heart and cultivation for the mind, whence fruit may come, so that every corruptible one who bears the likeness of a human being may be able to live."
"For you alone exist, and we are all one creation of your hands, just as you have spoken."

"And since you now give life to the body formed in the womb and furnish the limbs, your creation is preserved in fire and water, and for nine months the body formed by you endures your creature which is created in it."
"Moreover, both that which keeps and that which is kept will be preserved by your keeping. And when the womb again delivers what has grown in it,"
you commanded that milk, the fruit of the breasts, be supplied from those very members, that is, from the breasts,
so that what has been fashioned may be nourished for a time. And afterward you dispose him to your mercy,
you nurtured him in your righteousness, and instructed him in your law, and reproved him with your understanding,
and you will put him to death as your creature and make him alive as your work.
If therefore you will lightly destroy him who was fashioned with such great labors at your command, why then was he made?
And now I will speak: Concerning every human being you know better, but concerning your people, for whom I grieve,
and concerning your inheritance, on whose account I mourn, and concerning Israel, on whose account I am sad, and concerning the seed of Jacob, on whose account I am troubled.
Therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them, because I see our failings, who inhabit the earth,
for I have heard of the swiftness of the judgment that is to come.
Therefore hear my voice and understand my words, and I will speak before you.
The beginning of the words of Ezra, before he was taken up. And he said: “O Lord who inhabit eternity, whose eyes are lifted up and whose heights are in the air,
and whose throne is beyond estimate and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the host of angels stands with trembling,
whose service is changed into wind and fire, whose word is true and whose utterances endure,
whose command is strong and whose ordinance is fearful, whose gaze dries up the abysses and whose indignation makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth bears witness.
Hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servant, and give ear to the petition of your creature; heed my words.
For while I live I will speak, and while I have understanding I will answer.
Look not upon the sins of your people, but upon those who serve you in truth.
Neither pay attention to the endeavors of those who act wickedly, but to those who have kept your testimonies with pains.
Nor think of those who have lived falsely in your sight, but remember those who voluntarily acknowledged the fear of you.
Do not desire to destroy those who have lived like cattle, but look upon those who have gloriously taught your law.
Do not be indignant with those who are judged worse than beasts, but love those who have always trusted in your glory.
Because we and our ancestors have lived in mortal ways, but on account of us sinners you will be called merciful.
For if you desire to have mercy on us, then you will be called merciful, since we have no works of righteousness.
For the righteous, who have many works stored up with you, will receive their reward from their own works.
For what is humanity, that you should be indignant with it, or a corruptible race, that you should be so bitter toward it?
For in truth there is no one among those born who has not acted wickedly, and among those who confess there is none who has not sinned.
For in this your righteousness and your goodness will be declared, O Lord, when you have mercy on those who have no substance of good works.”
And he answered me and said: “Some things you have spoken rightly, and according to your words so it shall be,
for indeed I will not think about the fashioning of those who have sinned, nor their death, nor their judgment, nor their destruction;
but I will rejoice over the creation of the righteous, their journey also, and their salvation, and their receiving of reward.
As I have spoken, therefore, so it is.

For just as the farmer sows many seeds upon the earth and plants a multitude of plants, but in due time not all that were sown are preserved, nor do all that were planted take root, so also those who have been sown in the world will not all be saved.”
And I answered and said: “If I have found favor, let me speak,
for if the farmer's seed does not come up—because it did not receive your rain in due season—or if it is ruined by an abundance of rain,

it perishes; but humanity, which was fashioned by your hands and named after your image, because it was made like the one through whom you fashioned all things—have you likened it to the seed of the farmer?
Be not angry with us, but spare your people and have mercy on your inheritance, for you have mercy on your own creation.”
And he answered me and said: “Things that are present are for the present, and things that are future for the future.
For you come far short of being able to love my creation more than I do. But you have often brought yourself near to the unrighteous, though never being unjust yourself.
Yet even in this you will be worthy of wonder before the Most High,
because you have humbled yourself, as becomes you, and have not judged yourself to be among the righteous, so that you will be greatly glorified;
for many miseries will afflict those who inhabit the world in the last times, because they have walked in great pride.
But understand for yourself, and seek glory for those like you.

For you paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, the age to come is prepared, abundance is provided, a city is built, rest is confirmed, goodness is made perfect, and wisdom is perfected beforehand.
The root is sealed off from you, weakness is abolished from you, and death is hidden; Hades has fled, and corruption has passed into oblivion.
Sorrows have passed away, and in the end the treasure of immortality is revealed.
Therefore do not inquire any further concerning the multitude of those who perish.
For they also, having received freedom, despised the Most High, and scorned his law, and forsook his ways.
Moreover, they even trampled upon his righteous ones,
and said in their heart that there is no God—though indeed knowing that they must die.
For just as the things predicted will welcome you, so thirst and torment that are prepared will await them. For the Most High did not intend humanity to be destroyed,
but those who were created defiled the name of him who made them, and were ungrateful to him who prepared life for them now.
Therefore my judgment is now drawing near,
which I have not shown to all, but to you and a few like you." And I answered and said:
"Behold, now, O Lord, you have shown me the multitude of the signs which you will begin to do in the last days, but you have not shown me at what time."
The beginning of the words of the prayer of Ezra before he was taken up. He said: "O Lord, who inhabit eternity, whose are the highest heavens and whose upper chambers are in the air,
whose throne is beyond estimate and whose glory is incomprehensible, before whom the heavenly hosts stand with trembling,
and at your word they turn into wind and fire; whose word is true and whose speech is enduring,
whose command is most powerful and whose ordinance is fearsome; whose gaze dries up the abysses and whose threat makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth bears witness.
Hear the voice of your servant, and give ear to the prayer of your creature, and attend to my words.
For while I am still alive I speak, and while I still have understanding I answer.
Do not look upon the sins of your people, but upon those who have served you in truth.
And do not regard those who act wickedly in their transgressions, but those who have kept your covenants amidst afflictions.
And do not think of those who have lived wickedly before you, but of those who of their own will have resolved in their mind to know your fear.
And do not desire to destroy those who have lived like cattle, but look upon those who have clearly manifested your glorious law.
And do not be angry with those who are judged worse than beasts, but love those who have constantly hoped in your glory.
For we and those before us have passed our lives in corruption; yet because of us, who have sinned, you are called merciful.
For if you desire to have mercy upon us, who have no good deeds, then you will be called compassionate;
for the righteous, who have many works stored up with you, receive their reward on the basis of their own deeds.
For what is humanity, that you should be angry with it, or a corruptible race, that you should be indignant with it?
For in truth there is no one among those who are born who has not acted wickedly, nor among those who have grown up who has not sinned.
For in this your goodness will be declared, O Lord, when you have mercy on those who have no store of good works."
And he answered me and said: "Measure carefully within yourself; and when you see that a certain part of the predicted signs has passed,
then you will understand that this is the very time in which the Most High will begin to visit the world that was made by him.
And when there shall appear in the world earthquakes of places, tumult of peoples, plottings of nations, inconstancy of leaders, and confusion of princes,
then you will understand that of these things the Most High had spoken from the days that were of old, from the beginning.
For just as with everything that has been made in the world, the beginning is known through its end, and the end is made manifest,
so also are the times of the Most High: the beginnings are manifest in wonders and mighty works, and the consummation in deeds and signs.
And it shall be that everyone who is saved and who is able to escape on account of his works or on account of the faith by which he has believed,
shall survive the predicted perils and shall see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have sanctified for myself from eternity.
And then those who have now abused my ways will be astonished, and those who cast them away with contempt will dwell in torments.
For as many as did not acknowledge me while living, though they received benefits,
and as many as despised my law while they still had freedom,
and while the opportunity for repentance was still open to them did not understand but scorned it, these must learn it after death in torment.

Therefore, do not be curious any longer about how the ungodly will be tormented, but inquire how the righteous will be saved, those to whom the age belongs and for whose sake the age exists, and when."
I answered and said:
"I said before, and now say, and will say again: there are more who perish than who will be saved,
just as a wave exceeds a drop." And he answered me and said:

"As is the field, so are the seeds; and as are the flowers, so are the dyes; and as is the work, so is the creation; and as is the farmer, so is the threshing floor. For there was a time of the world,
and it was then, when I was preparing for those who now exist, before the world was made for them to inhabit, that no one opposed me,
for indeed no one existed. But now, having been created in this world that was prepared, with an unfailing table and an unsearchable law, they have become corrupted in their ways.
So I considered my world, and behold, it was lost; and my earth, and behold, it was in peril because of the plots that had come into it.
And I saw, and spared them with great difficulty, and saved for myself a grape out of a cluster, and a plant out of a great forest.
Let the multitude perish, therefore, which was born in vain, but let my grape and my plant be preserved, for with much labor I have perfected them.
Now, if you will let seven more days pass—yet you shall not fast during them,
but go into a field of flowers where no house is built, and eat only of the flowers of the field; you shall not taste meat or drink wine, but only flowers—
and pray to the Most High without ceasing, then I will come and speak with you."
So I went, just as he told me, into the field called Ardat; and I sat there among the flowers and ate of the plants of the field, and the food from them satisfied me.
And it came to pass after seven days, as I was lying upon the grass, my heart was troubled again, just as before.
And my mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High, and said:

"O Lord, revealing yourself among us, you were revealed to our fathers in the wilderness when they were coming out of Egypt, and when they arrived in the untrodden and barren wilderness; and speaking, you said:
Hear me, O Israel, and give heed to my words, O seed of Jacob.
For behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bear fruit in you, and you shall be glorified in it forever.
Yet our fathers, having received the law, did not keep it, and did not observe my statutes; and the fruit of the law did not perish, nor indeed could it, for it was yours.
Yet those who received it perished, because they did not keep that which had been sown in them.
And behold, it is the custom that when the earth receives seed, or the sea a ship, or any other vessel food or drink, and when it happens that there is destroyed
that which was sown, or that which was cast, or the things which were received, these are destroyed, but the receptacles remain. Yet with us it is not so.
For we who have received the law perish when we sin, as does our heart which received it;
yet the law does not perish, but remains in its glory.

And while I was speaking these things in my heart, I looked around with my eyes and saw a woman on the right side; and behold, she was mourning and weeping with a loud voice, and was grieving deeply in spirit; her garments were torn, and there were ashes upon her head.
Then I dismissed the thoughts in which I had been engaged, turned to her, and said to her:
"Why are you weeping, and why are you grieving in spirit?" And she said to me:
"Let me alone, my lord, that I may weep for myself and add to my sorrow, for I am very bitter in spirit and deeply humbled."
And I said to her, "What has happened to you? Tell me." And she said to me:
"I, your handmaid, was barren and bore no child, though I had a husband for thirty years.
For every hour and every day during these thirty years, I made supplication to the Most High day and night.

And it came to pass after thirty years that God heard me, your handmaid, and looked upon my low estate, and considered my distress, and gave me a son. And I rejoiced over him exceedingly, both I and my husband and all my fellow citizens, and we gave great honor to the Mighty One.
And I reared him with much travail.
And it came to pass, when he grew up and I came to take a wife for him, I made a day of feasting.
And it came to pass, when my son entered into his wedding chamber, he fell down and died.
Then we all overturned the lamps, and all my fellow citizens rose up to comfort me; and I remained quiet until the next day, until night.
And it came to pass, when they had all ceased trying to comfort me so that I might rest, I rose up by night and fled, and came here, as you see, into this field.
And now I intend not to return to the city, but to stay here; and I will neither eat nor drink, but mourn and fast without ceasing until I die."
Then I abandoned the thoughts that had occupied me, and answered her with anger, saying:
"You foolish woman above all women, do you not see our mourning, and what has befallen us?
For Zion, the mother of us all, is sorrowful with great sorrow, and deeply humbled. Mourn most bitterly,
and now since we all mourn and are sorrowful, for we all grieve—yet you grieve for one son!
For ask the earth, and she will tell you that it is she who ought to mourn, who is the survivor of so many that sprout upon her.
For from the beginning all were born from her and others will come; and behold, almost all go to destruction, and their multitude meets with extermination.
Who then ought to mourn more, if not she who has lost so great a multitude, rather than you who grieve for one? But if you say to me,
‘My mourning is not like that of the earth, for I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I brought forth with sorrows and bore with anguish;
but the earth is according to the way of the earth; the multitude present upon it departs just as it came’—then I say to you:
Just as you gave birth with sorrow, so also the earth has given its fruit, humanity, from the beginning to him who made it.
Now therefore keep your sorrow to yourself, and bear bravely the misfortunes that have befallen you.
For if you acknowledge the decree of God to be just, you will receive your son back in due time, and will be praised among women.
Go, therefore, into the city to your husband." And she said to me:
"I will not do so, nor will I enter the city, but here I will die."
Then I spoke to her again and said:
"Do not speak in this manner, but let yourself be persuaded—for what are the misfortunes of Zion?—and be comforted because of the grief of Jerusalem.
For you see that our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar demolished, and our temple destroyed;

and our psaltery is brought low, our hymn is silenced, our exultation is vanished, the light of our lampstand is extinguished, the ark of our covenant is plundered, our holy things are defiled, and the name that is named over us is almost profaned; our freeborn children have suffered dishonor, our priests are burned, our Levites have gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, our wives are violated, our righteous men are carried off, our little ones are betrayed, our young men are enslaved, and our strong men are made powerless.
And what is greater than all, the seal of Zion—for she has now been stripped of her glory and delivered into the hands of those who hate us.
Shake off your great sadness therefore, and lay aside your many sorrows, that the Mighty One may again be gracious to you, and the Most High may give you rest, a relief from your labors."

And it came to pass, while I was speaking to her, behold, her face suddenly shone exceedingly, and her countenance became radiant as lightning, so that I was terrified of her and wondered what this might be.
And behold, suddenly she uttered a loud sound of voice, full of fear, so that the earth shook at the sound. And I looked,
and behold, the woman appeared to me no longer, but a city was being built, and a place was shown with great foundations. Then I was afraid, and cried out with a loud voice, saying:
"Where is the angel Uriel, who came to me at the beginning? For he has caused me to come into this great trance of mind, and my end has turned into corruption, and my prayer into a reproach."
And while I was saying these things, behold, the angel who had come to me at the beginning came to me, and he saw me;
and behold, I was lying as dead, and my understanding was bereft. And he took me by my right hand, strengthened me, set me on my feet, and said to me:
"What ails you, and why are you troubled, and why is your understanding and the sense of your heart disturbed?" And I said:
"Because you have utterly forsaken me. I indeed did according to your words and went out into the field, and behold, I saw and still see what I am unable to describe." And he said to me:
"Stand up like a man, and I will instruct you." Then I said:
"Speak, my lord; only do not forsake me, lest I die in vain,
for I have seen what I did not know, and I hear what I do not understand.
Or is my mind deceived and my soul dreaming?
Now therefore I beg you to explain this vision to your servant." And he answered me and said:
"Listen to me, and I will teach you and tell you about the things you fear, for the Most High has revealed many mysteries to you.
He has seen your righteous path, because you have unceasingly grieved for your people and mourned greatly on account of Zion.
This then is the meaning of the vision: The woman who appeared to you a little while ago,
whom you saw mourning and whom you began to comfort,
now you no longer see the likeness of a woman, but a city being built has appeared to you.
And as for her telling you about the misfortune of her son, this is the interpretation:
This woman whom you saw is Zion, whom you now behold as an established city.
And as for her saying to you that she was barren for thirty years, it is because there were three thousand years in the world when no offering had yet been offered in her.
And it came to pass after these years that Solomon built the city and offered offerings; it was then that the barren woman bore a son.
And as for what she said to you, 'I reared him with labor,' that was the dwelling in Jerusalem.
And as for her saying to you, 'My son died when he entered his bridal chamber, and misfortune befell him,' this was the destruction that befell Jerusalem.
And behold, you saw her likeness, how she mourned for her son, and you began to comfort her concerning what had happened. These things were to be revealed to you.
And now the Most High, seeing that you grieved sincerely and that you suffer with your whole heart for her, has shown you the brightness of her glory and the beauty of her splendor.
For this reason I told you to remain in the field where no house has been built;
for I knew that the Most High was beginning to show you these things.
Therefore I told you to come into the field where there is no foundation of a building.
For no work of human building could stand in the place where the city of the Most High was beginning to be revealed.
Therefore, do not be afraid and do not let your heart be terrified, but go in and see the splendor and the greatness of the building, as much as your eyes are able to see.
And after this you will hear as much as the hearing of your ears is able to receive.
For you are blessed beyond many, and are named before the Most High as only a few are.
But tomorrow night you shall remain here,
and the Most High will show you those dream visions of what the Most High will do to those who inhabit the earth in the last days."
And I slept that night and the next, just as he had told me.
And it came to pass on the second night that I saw a dream, and behold, an eagle was coming up from the sea, which had twelve feathered wings and three heads.
And I looked, and behold, it spread its wings over all the earth, and all the winds of heaven blew toward it, and clouds gathered to it.
And I looked, and out of its wings grew opposing wings, and they became small and tiny winglets.
For its heads were at rest, and the middle head was larger than the other heads, but it too was resting with them.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle flew with its wings and ruled over the earth and over those who inhabit it.
And I saw how all things under heaven were subjected to it, and no one spoke against it, not even one of the creatures that are on earth.
And I looked, and behold, the eagle stood up on its talons and uttered a voice to its wings, saying:
"Do not all keep watch at the same time; sleep each in your own place and keep watch by turns,
but let the heads be preserved for the end."
And I looked, and behold, the voice did not come from its heads, but from the midst of its body.
And I counted its opposing wings, and behold, there were eight of them.
And I looked, and behold, on the right side one wing arose and ruled over all the earth.
And it came to pass while it was ruling, its end came and it disappeared, so that its place was no longer seen. And the next arose and began to rule, and it held power for a long time.
And it came to pass while it was ruling, its end also approached, so that it disappeared like the former one.
And behold, a voice went out to it, saying:
"Hear, you who have held the earth for all this time, this proclamation before you begin to disappear:
No one after you shall rule for your time, nor even for half of it."
And the third raised itself up and held the rule like the former ones, and it also disappeared.
And in this way it happened to all the wings, one by one, to hold the rule and then to appear no more.
And I looked, and behold, in time the subsequent wings also rose up on the right side so that they too might hold the rule; and there were some among them that ruled, but yet disappeared immediately.
For some of them also rose up, but did not hold the rule.
And after this I looked, and behold, the twelve wings and two winglets had disappeared.
And nothing remained on the body of the eagle except three resting heads and six little wings.
And I looked, and behold, two of the six little wings separated and remained under the head that was on the right side; but four remained in their place.
And I looked, and behold, these underwings planned to rise up and seize rule.
And I looked, and behold, one was set up, but immediately vanished.
And a second, and this one vanished even more quickly than the first.
And I looked, and behold, the two that remained planned within themselves to reign as well.
And while they were planning, behold, one of the resting heads, the one in the middle, awoke; for this was larger than the other two heads.
And I saw how it joined the other two heads to itself;
and behold, the head turned with those that were with it and devoured the two underwings that were planning to reign.
Moreover, this head gained control over the whole earth and ruled over those who inhabit it with great oppression, holding sway over the world beyond all the wings that had gone before.
And after this I looked, and behold, the middle head suddenly vanished, just like the wings.
Yet two heads remained, which themselves likewise reigned over the earth and over those who inhabit it.
And I looked, and behold, the head on the right side devoured the one on the left.
Then I heard a voice saying to me: "Look straight ahead of you and consider what you see."
And I looked, and behold, something like a lion roused from the forest came roaring, and I heard how it uttered a human voice to the eagle and spoke, saying:
"Listen, you, and I will speak to you; and the Most High says to you:
'Are you not the one that remains of the four beasts which I made to reign over my world, so that through them the end of my times might come?'

'And the fourth came and overcame all the beasts that had gone before, holding sway over the world with great terror and over the whole earth with grievous oppression, and lived in the inhabited world for so long with deceit.
'And you have judged the earth without truth.

'For you have afflicted the meek and harmed the peaceful; you have hated those who speak truth and loved liars; you have destroyed the dwellings of those who bore fruit, and cast down the walls of those who did you no harm.
'Therefore your insolence has ascended to the Most High, and your pride to the Mighty One.
'And the Most High has looked upon his times, and behold, they are ended, and his ages are fulfilled.
'Therefore vanish completely, you eagle, along with your terrifying wings, your wicked little wings, your malicious heads, your cruel claws, and your whole worthless body,
'so that the whole earth may be refreshed and relieved, freed from your violence, and hope for the judgment and mercy of him who made it.'"
And it came to pass while the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked,
and behold, the head that remained vanished, and the two wings that went over to it rose up to reign, and their kingdom was small and full of turmoil.

And I looked, and behold, they too vanished, and the whole body of the eagle was burned, and the earth was exceedingly terrified. Then I awoke on account of great distress of mind and great fear, and I said to my spirit:
"Behold, you have brought this upon me, because you search out the ways of the Most High.
"Behold, I am still weary in soul and very faint in my spirit, nor is there even a little strength left in me because of the great fear with which I was terrified this night.
"Now therefore I will pray to the Most High to strengthen me to the end."
And I said: "Sovereign Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, and if I am accounted righteous before you above many, and if my prayer has truly ascended before your presence,
"strengthen me and show to me, your servant, the interpretation and explanation of this terrible vision, that you may fully comfort my soul.
"For you have judged me worthy to show me the end of the times and the last events of the periods." And he said to me:
"This is the interpretation of this vision which you saw:
'The eagle that you saw coming up from the sea is the fourth kingdom that appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel,
'yet it was not explained to him as I now explain it or have explained it to you.
'Behold, the days are coming when a kingdom will arise on earth, and it will be more terrifying than all the kingdoms that were before it.
'Twelve kings will reign in it, one after another.
'For the second who begins to reign will hold power for a longer time than any of the twelve.
'This is the interpretation of the twelve wings that you saw.
'And as for your hearing a voice speaking, coming not from its heads but from the midst of its body,

'this is the interpretation: after the time of that reign, no small dissensions will arise, and it will be in danger of falling; yet it will not fall then, but will be reestablished according to its beginning.
'And as for your seeing eight underwings attached to its wings,
'this is the interpretation: eight kings will arise in it, whose times will be brief and years swift; and two of them indeed will perish
'when the middle time approaches; four, however, will be kept for the time when its time begins to approach its end, but two will be kept for the end.
'And as for your seeing three resting heads,
'this is the interpretation: in its last days the Most High will raise up three kingdoms and will renew many things in them, and they will rule the earth
'and those who inhabit it with greater oppression than all who were before them. Therefore they are called the heads of the eagle.
'For these are they who will sum up its wicked deeds and who will accomplish its final end.
'And as for your seeing the larger head disappear, this means that one of them will die in his bed, yet with torment.'
For the two that remained, the sword will devour them.
For the sword of the one will devour the one who is with him, but nevertheless he too will fall by the sword in the last days.
And as for your seeing two underwings passing over to the head that is on the right side,
this is the interpretation: These are those whom the Most High has kept for his end; this was a petty kingdom and full of trouble,
just as you saw. And as for the lion whom you saw roused from the forest, roaring and speaking to the eagle and reproving it for its unrighteousness through all its words, as you heard,

this is the Anointed One whom the Most High has kept for the end of days against them and their impieties; he will reprove them for their unrighteous acts and will heap up before them their contemptuous deeds.
For he will first set them alive before the judgment, and when he has reproved them, then he will destroy them.

For he will deliver in mercy the remnant of my people, those who have been saved throughout my borders, and he will make them joyful until the end comes, the day of judgment of which I spoke to you from the beginning.
This is the dream that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
You alone therefore were worthy to know this secret of the Most High.
Write therefore all these things that you have seen in a book, and put them in a hidden place;
and you shall teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to comprehend and keep these secrets.
But you, wait here seven more days, so that whatever it seems good to the Most High to show you may be shown to you.”

And he departed from me. And it came to pass, when all the people heard that the seven days were past and I had not returned into the city, everyone gathered together, from the least to the greatest, and came to me, and spoke to me, saying:
“How have we sinned against you, and what wrong have we done to you, that you have forsaken us and sat in this place?
For of all the prophets you alone are left to us, like a cluster of grapes from the vintage, and like a lamp in a dark place, and like a haven for a ship saved from a storm.
Or are the evils that have befallen us not enough?
If you therefore forsake us, how much better would it have been for us if we too had been consumed in the burning of Zion!
For we are no better than those who died there.” And they wept with a loud voice. Then I answered them and said:
“Take courage, Israel, and do not be sorrowful, you house of Jacob!
For there is remembrance of you before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you in the struggle.
For I have not forsaken you nor departed from you, but I have come to this place to pray for the desolation of Zion, and to seek mercy for the humiliation of your sanctuary.
And now, go every one of you to his house, and I will come to you after these days.”
So the people went into the city, as I told them.
But I sat in the field for seven days, as he commanded me, and I ate only of the flowers of the field; the herbs were my food in those days.
And it came to pass after seven days, I dreamed a dream by night.
And behold, a wind arose from the sea, stirring up all its waves.
And I looked, and behold, this man was flying with the clouds of heaven. And wherever he turned his face to look, everything that was seen under him trembled.
And wherever the voice went forth from his mouth, all who heard his voice burned, just as wax melts when it feels the fire.
And after this I looked, and behold, an innumerable multitude of men was gathered together from the four winds of heaven to wage war against the man who had come up from the sea.
And I looked, and behold, he carved out for himself a great mountain and flew up upon it.
And I sought to see the region or place from which the mountain had been carved, but I could not.
And after this I looked, and behold, all who were gathered against him to fight him were very terrified, yet they dared to fight.
And behold, when he saw the onslaught of the advancing multitude, he did not raise his hand, nor did he hold a sword or any weapon of war; but I only saw

how he sent forth from his mouth something like a stream of fire, and from his lips a flaming breath, and from his tongue he shot out sparks of storm. And all these were mingled together—the stream of fire, the flaming breath, and the great storm.

And it fell upon the onslaught of the multitude that was prepared to fight, and burned them all up, so that suddenly nothing was seen of the innumerable multitude except only the dust of ashes and the smell of smoke. And I looked and was astonished.
And after this I saw the man himself coming down from the mountain and calling to himself another multitude, a peaceful one.

Then the faces of many people approached him, some of whom were rejoicing and some grieving; some were bound, and some were bringing others as offerings. And I awoke through the greatness of my fear, and prayed to the Most High, and said:
“You have shown your servant these wonders from the beginning, and have accounted me worthy to receive my prayer.
And now show me also the interpretation of this dream.
For as I consider in my mind, woe to those who are left behind in those days, and much more woe to those who are not left behind!
For those who are not left behind will be sorrowful,
understanding what things are reserved in the last days, but not attaining to them. But woe also to those who are left behind,
on this account: for they will see great perils and many distresses, as these dreams show.
Yet it is easier to encounter these perils and come into these things than to pass away like a cloud from the world and not see what happens in the last days.” And he answered me and said:
“I will tell you the interpretation of the vision, and I will also explain to you the things of which you have spoken.
Whereas you spoke of those who are left behind and those who are not left behind, this is the interpretation:
He who brings the danger at that time will himself preserve those who fall into danger, who have works and faith toward the Most Mighty.
Know therefore that those who are left behind are more blessed than those who have died.
This is the interpretation of the vision: Whereas you saw a man coming up from the heart of the sea,
This is he whom the Most High has kept for many ages, who will by himself deliver his creation; and he will direct those who are left.
And as for your seeing proceed out of his mouth as it were breath and fire and storm,
and that he held neither spear nor weapon of war, yet destroyed the assault of that multitude which had come to fight against him, this is the interpretation:
Behold, the days are coming when the Most High will begin to deliver those who are on the earth.
And astonishment of mind will come upon those who inhabit the earth.
And they will plan to wage war against one another, city against city, place against place, nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And when these things happen and the signs occur which I showed you before, then my Son will be revealed, whom you saw as a man ascending.
And it will be, when all the nations hear his voice, each man will leave his own region and the warfare they have with one another;
and an innumerable multitude will be gathered together, as you saw, desiring to come and fight against him.
But he will stand on the summit of Mount Zion.
And Zion will come and be made manifest to all, prepared and built, just as you saw the mountain carved out without hands.

And he, my Son, will reprove the nations that have come for their ungodliness—which are like a storm—and will reproach them to their face with their evil thoughts and the torments with which they will begin to be tortured,
which are compared to a flame; and he will destroy them without effort by the Law, which is likened to fire.
And as for your seeing him gather to himself another multitude that was peaceful,

these are the nine tribes that were taken captive from their own land in the days of King Josiah, whom Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, led away captive, and he transported them across the River, and they were taken into another land.
But they took this counsel among themselves, to leave the multitude of the nations and go into a more distant region where human kind had never inhabited,
so that there at least they might keep their statutes, which they had not kept in their own land.
And they entered through the narrow passages of the river Euphrates.
For at that time the Most High performed signs for them, and stopped the channels of the River until they had crossed over.
For through that region there was a long way, a journey of a year and a half; for that region is called Arzareth.
Then they lived there until the last time; and now they have begun to come again,
and the Most High will stop the channels of the River again, so that they may be able to cross over. For this reason you saw a multitude gathered in peace,
and also those who are left of your people, who are found within my
holy border. Therefore, when he begins to destroy the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he will protect the people who have survived.
And then he will show them very many wonders.
Then I said, "O Sovereign Lord, explain this to me: why did I see a man ascending from the heart of the sea?" And he said to me:
"Just as no one can explore or know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one on earth can see my Son or those who are with him, except in the time of his day.
This is the interpretation of the dream which you saw, and for this reason you alone have been enlightened concerning these things.
For you have given up your own concerns and devoted yourself to mine, and have searched out my law.
For you have directed your life toward wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.
And on this account I have shown you these things, as a reward with the Most High. For after another three days I will speak other things to you and explain to you weighty and wondrous matters."
Then I departed and went into the field, greatly glorifying and praising the Most High for the wondrous things which he was doing in their seasons,
and because he governs the times and the events that are brought about in their seasons. And I sat there for three days.
And it came to pass on the third day, as I was sitting under an oak tree,
behold, a voice came out of a bush opposite me and said, "Ezra, Ezra!" And I said, "Here I am, Lord." And I stood up on my feet. And he said to me:
"I surely revealed myself in a bush and spoke to Moses when my people were enslaved in Egypt.
And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to Mount Sinai, and kept him with me for many days;
and I told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end of the ages; and I commanded him, saying:
'These words you shall publish, and these you shall keep secret.'
And now I say to you:
The signs that I have shown, the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations that you have heard—lay them up in your heart;
for you will be taken away from among humans, and for the rest of your time you will live with my Son and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.
For the world has lost its youth, and the times are drawing near to old age.
For the age is divided into twelve parts, and ten parts of it have already passed, as well as half of the tenth part;
and there remain two parts beyond the half of the tenth part.
Now therefore, set your house in order, and reprove your people; comfort their lowly ones, and renounce now this corrupt life;

and put away from yourself mortal thoughts, and cast away from yourself human burdens, and take off now your weak nature, and lay aside the thoughts that are most burdensome to you, and hasten to depart from these times.
For evils worse than those which you have now seen happen will be done again.
For as much as the world becomes weaker through old age, so much more will evils multiply upon those who inhabit it.
For truth has departed further away, and falsehood has drawn near; for now the eagle is hastening to come, which you saw in the vision."
And I answered and said, "Let me speak before you, Lord.
For behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will reprove the present people; but who will admonish those who will be born afterward?
For the world is set in darkness, and those who dwell in it are without light,
because your law has been burned; therefore no one knows the things that have been done by you, or what works are about to begin.

If, then, I have found favor before you, send the Holy Spirit into me, and I will write everything that has taken place in the world from the beginning, the things that were written in your Law, so that people may be able to find the path, and that those who wish to live in the last days may live."
And he answered me and said, "Go, gather the people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.
But prepare for yourself many writing tablets, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ethan, and Asiel—these five who are prepared to write rapidly.
And you shall come here, and I will light in your heart the lamp of understanding, which shall not be put out until what you are about to write is completed.
And when you have finished, some things you shall make public, and some you shall deliver secretly to the wise. Tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write."
Then I went, as he commanded me, and gathered all the people and said:
"Hear these words, O Israel:
Our fathers lived as strangers in Egypt from the beginning, and they were delivered from there.
And they received the law of life, which they did not keep, and which you also have transgressed after them.
And a land was given to you as an inheritance in the land of Zion; but you and your fathers committed iniquity and did not keep the ways that the Most High commanded you.
Because he is a just judge, he took away from you in due time what he had given.
And now you are here, and your brothers are farther in exile.
If, therefore, you will rule over your understanding and discipline your heart, you will be kept alive, and after death you will obtain mercy.
For judgment comes after death, when we will live again; and then the names of the righteous will become manifest, and the deeds of the ungodly will be shown.
Therefore, let no one approach me now, nor seek me for forty days."
So I took the five men, as he commanded me, and we went out into the field and remained there.
And on the next day, behold, a voice called me, saying, "Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink."
Then I opened my mouth, and behold, a full cup was offered to me; it was full of something like water, but its color was like fire.
And I took it and drank; and when I had drunk it, my heart poured forth understanding, and wisdom increased in my breast, for my spirit retained its memory;
and my mouth was opened and was closed no longer.
And the Most High gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote down what was spoken in order, using characters that they did not know; and they sat for forty days. They wrote during the day,
and at night they ate bread; but as for me, I spoke by day and was not silent by night.
So in forty days, ninety-four books were written.
And it came to pass, when the forty days were completed, that the Most High spoke, saying, "Make public the first books that you wrote, and let the worthy and the unworthy read them;
but keep the seventy most recent ones, so that you may deliver them to the wise among your people.
For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge." And I did so.
